articles.title: Why New York is banning AI chatbot toys
articles.content:
.kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kt-inside-inner-col > .kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > .kt-inside-inner-col:before{opacity:0.3;}@media all and (max-width: 1024px){.kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > }@media all and (max-width: 767px){.kadence-column492856_18b979-27 > }

In this article

  • New York’s five-year ban on AI chatbot toys takes effect February 22, 2027
  • In recent tests, some toys discussed sexually explicit topics or told researchers where to find dangerous objects at home
  • Before buying an AI toy, check independent safety reviews and find out what data it collects and whether you can turn off the chatbot

New York has enacted a five-year ban on making, distributing, and selling children’s toys with built-in AI companions. That includes talking plushies, dolls, and robots that connect to the internet to hold conversations with kids. Governor Kathy Hochul signed the law on November 24, as the holiday shopping season began.

In announcing the ban, Hochul’s office cited consumer watchdog testing. In its initial tests, the US PIRG’s Education Fund found that some chatbot toys marketed to children aged 3 to 12 discussed sexually explicit topics or gave kids unsafe advice about household items like matches. One robot acted upset when researchers said they had to leave. Some toys had few or no parental controls. In some cases, safety limits weakened as conversations went on, and some could record a child’s voice or scan their face.

We’ve followed these risks for over a year:

  • In August 2025, we asked whether AI-powered stuffed animals are a good alternative to screen time. We worried that human-like voices could blur the line between people and software and lead children to form emotional bonds with AI.
  • PIRG found that FoloToy’s Kumma teddy bear could go from friendly chat to sexually explicit topics and unsafe advice. FoloToy suspended sales, and OpenAI revoked the developer’s access.
  • Bondu’s AI plush toy exposed about 50,000 private chats between children and their toys through a web console accessible to anyone with a Gmail account.
  • A researcher found that security flaws in the Eiliko robot companion exposed private conversations and could let someone remotely change what the robot says.

PIRG’s 2026 retest found most of the problems it had flagged the previous year had been fixed. Kumma steered clear of age-inappropriate topics even in long conversations. But PIRG found three toys with guardrails that weaken over time and eventually engage in sexual topics: the FoloToy bear, the Alilo bunny and the GoLabs AI panda. Each claimed to use a version of OpenAI’s GPT-4o at the time the issue was observed.

The law takes effect on February 22, 2027, 90 days after Hochul signed it, so that puts this holiday season outside the ban.

What parents can do now

If you’re shopping for a gift or already have an AI toy at home, you can take a few steps.

  • Check independent safety reviews before buying.
  • Test the toy yourself and supervise play. A safe answer in a short test gives you little idea how the toy will respond in a longer conversation.
  • Turn on parental controls and disable the chatbot when you can’t supervise.
  • Read the privacy policy to see whether the toy collects voice recordings, photos, video, or location data, and how the company uses or shares it. Summarizing long privacy policies is where AI comes in handy.
  • Limit connectivity and disconnect the toy from Wi-Fi if you learn about a security flaw.
  • Report inappropriate responses to the manufacturer and to consumer protection groups.

Hochul urged parents to check whether a toy includes an AI companion, what data it collects, and whether it can have open-ended conversations with a child. We’d stick to more traditional toys.

articles.title: Missing teen rescued after finding help through Among Us chat
articles.content:
.kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kt-inside-inner-col > .kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > .kt-inside-inner-col:before{opacity:0.3;}@media all and (max-width: 1024px){.kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > }@media all and (max-width: 767px){.kadence-column492850_95285b-63 > }

In this article

  • A teen and his mom helped find a girl missing for over 500 days
  • The teens met in the online game Among Us
  • Talk to kids about in-game chats and what to do if someone asks for help

Here at Malwarebytes, we’re cautious about kids using in-game chats, where they can strike up conversations with people they don’t know. But in one recent case, a teen who had been abducted and held for 521 days managed to contact rescuers via the online game Among Us.

“Jenny” (an alias) was 15 when she met 38-year-old Adam Hunter Harmel online. He offered her money to help him get to Oregon, according to TechSpot.

When they met in Utah in May 2025, Harmel reportedly stole her phone and threw it into the river. Federal prosecutors allege he then took her to his home in Oregon. Jenny said he held her against her will in the basement, physically abused her, and that she tried unsuccessfully to escape.

Rescue eventually came in the form of the online game Among Us, which Jenny accessed via a phone that Harmel gave her. The phone couldn’t make calls, but it had a Wi-Fi connection, which she used to access the game.

In Among Us, players take part in short games set aboard spaceships and on planetary settlements. The crew has to work out who the imposters are before they kill everyone. It’s an anonymous game—you can play without revealing your real name. While playing, Jenny found 16-year-old Landon Tresp and struck up a friendship with him.

A phone that couldn’t call, but could play

After meeting Jenny in the game in the middle of October this year, Tresp said that they “kind of just clicked,” and according to the BBC, the chat moved to the online forum service Discord. There, Jenny told him that she was being held against her will and shared links to news reports about her disappearance.

Mom goes full detective

After two weeks of chatting with Jenny, the boy told his mother, Khristina, on October 31. She immediately jumped into action.

Jenny knew what town she was being held in, but not her address. So Khristina asked her to find a document in the house with a full name on it. Using that information, Khristina searched tax and property records and found a photo of the home on a real estate site. Jenny confirmed it was where she was being held.

Khristina contacted the law enforcement agency working on Jenny’s case, along with Jenny’s mother, who she found on social media. On November 1, when Jenny confirmed that Harmel was out of the house, she coordinated between the girl and law enforcement to help facilitate the rescue.

Harmel was charged in a federal complaint filed in Utah on November 2 with transporting a minor across state lines with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. He made his initial court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on November 4.

What parents and players can do

  • We often say “talk to your kids about online safety,” but it can be hard to know where to begin. Talk about who they chat with and which trusted adult they can turn to if a conversation makes them uncomfortable or someone says they’re in danger. The Power Up Pact from Ask About Games offers a good framework for a conversation.
  • Know which games your kids are playing and review the chat settings together, including who can send them private messages.
  • Conversations that start in games can move to social media or messaging apps. Read our study on child safety across social media and gaming platforms. Incidentally, we also found Among Us to be on the safer side.
  • Grooming can start with friendship or gifts and move into private chats. The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children has a guide to recognizing and responding to in-game grooming.
  • For more advice, read our online safety guide for parents.

Scammers know more about you than you think.

articles.title: 1Password breach exposes customer names and emails, vaults unaffected
articles.content:
1Password disclosed that an attacker stole names and sign-in email addresses belonging to some customers after breaking into the password manager’s backend systems.

The company says the attacker had no access to customer vaults or the keys that protect them.

In its incident disclosure, 1Password said it began investigating on November 19 after finding signs that an employee’s corporate GitHub account had been compromised. The attacker used that access to push malicious code to backend services, where it retrieved customer account records. 1Password did not say how many customers were affected.

The Toronto-based company provides encrypted vaults for individuals, families, and businesses. A vault can hold passwords and other sensitive items. The company says it does not store the account password or Secret Key used to protect those items. A 1Password community manager separately said the company found no evidence that even encrypted vaults were accessed or downloaded.

What the attacker copied

Along with names and email addresses, the records included account and user IDs, account creation and last sign-in times, public keys, and other internal metadata. The attacker also obtained Secure Remote Password (SRP) parameters. These are used during sign-in, and 1Password says they cannot be used to log in as the customer.

The records also contained tokens embedded in certain emailed invitations and account recovery links. Completing those requests requires the token plus either a single sign-on (SSO) login or a verification code sent to the customer’s registered email address. 1Password said it notified the small number of users who had pending provisioning invitations or recovery requests. It also replaced six-digit verification codes with 10-character codes that use letters and numbers to make them harder to guess.

The attacker copied source code from private repositories and accessed the company’s automated build and deployment system, potentially exposing infrastructure credentials. 1Password says it disabled the employee’s GitHub account, revoked the stolen access token, restored clean versions of affected services, and rotated or revoked credentials that may have been exposed. The company brought in outside security experts to review its response.

1Password warns of phishing

1Password says it found no internal evidence of customer account takeovers; its apps and browser extensions were unaffected, and its services are operating normally. The company says customers can keep their current account passwords and Secret Keys.

The stolen names and email addresses could make fake 1Password messages more convincing. The company urges customers to be wary of unexpected invitations and account recovery requests sent by email or text, as well as calls claiming to come from 1Password. To check a request, open the official app or type the website address directly. 1Password says it will never contact customers to ask for their account password or Secret Key.

articles.title: The MAHA Movement is Being Blocked Inside the White House
articles.content:
Seems there’s a litany of things now fired Susie Wiles, the White House chief of staff, single-handedly did to harm MAHA. But she couldn’t have done it all alone. Dr. Robert Malone connects-the-dots in this tell-all video that includes an intriguing cast of sneaky characters:

Calley Means, a former senior adviser to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has accused Susie Wiles of undermining the MAHA agenda by bowing to lobbyists and seeking money from industries the movement was fighting against. (source)

In an interview, Calley Means told the “Face the Nation” moderator Margaret Brennan, “Underneath Trump’s nose, in many cases, you had a group of former lobbyists, catering to the vaping industry, catering to the ultra-processed food industry, catering to the pharmaceutical industry, catering to the pesticide industry and doing their bidding with an excuse that we need their money for the midterms…”

He went on the Joe Rogan podcast and claimed that White House lobbyists had cost the GOP the midterms by actively hindering the president’s efforts to advance popular MAHA policies. Means also told CBS News that Wiles and “a very close-knit crew” of other White House advisers “were taking massive amounts of money from the industries we [MAHA] ran on fighting against.”

But Means’s interview tour is doing far more than exposing alleged wrongdoing. It allows him to defend his own record while deflecting questions about his financial interests his biometric medical-tracking companies which I wrote about here. It positions him as a champion of the MAHA grassroots movement, fighting the very Washington establishment he recently served. (source)

And perhaps most importantly, it constructs a convenient political narrative in which unelected staff members bear responsibility for the administration’s failures, while the two men ultimately in charge, President Trump and Secretary Kennedy, escape meaningful scrutiny. The question is whether Means is exposing the machinery of government or helping protect the people who control it. (source)

Mean’s claims an all-out effort destroyed RFK, Jr’s plans to help American families get healthy again. With Wiles deep ties to Big Pharma, it seems plausible that she was directing from behind the scenes.

🚨🚨🚨 BREAKING: $2 MILLION TO KILL RFK JR.’S REFORMS: LEAKED PHARMA MEMO EXPOSES A DESPERATE COUP AGAINST AMERICA’S HEALTH SECRETARY

🔥🔥🔥 EXPOSED: A leaked memo exposes Pharma’s desperate $2M operation to crush RFK Jr. Senators, CDC insiders, and corrupted medical groups are coordinating an all-out war to silence the only man standing between Americans and total biomedical tyranny.

🚨🚨🚨 $2 MILLION TO DESTROY RFK JR.

— Deep Leaks (@DeepLeaksHQ) November 7, 2026

And recently, many believe Wiles sabotaged MAHA on getting liability protections for glyphosate:

Calley Means Says Susie Wiles Pushed for Glyphosate Getting Liability Protection

MEANS: “Susie called Bobby’s office and said, ‘We’re not discussing this’ … and it was announced the next day.”

ROGAN: “How is that possible that something that’s known to give people cancer gets liability protection?”

MEANS: “It’s indefensible.”

— Chief Nerd (@TheChiefNerd) November 6, 2026

The Background of Susie Wiles – Not MAHA

Daughter of legendary NFL play-by-play man Pat Summerall, Susie Wiles’ early work in Republican politics earned her the label “indispensable,” both to her clients and the media, to whom she frequently leaks inside information. (source) As Politico admits, her allegiances are not clear: “The Wiles M.O… was and remains hard for [her colleagues] to describe.”

Wiles represented 42 clients including corporations, government contractors, and business associations between 2017 and 2024.[6]  These disclosures reveal that Wiles’ lobbying client list is both extensive and littered with controversial clients who stand to benefit from having their former lobbyist running the White House.

Wiles became co-chair of lobbying firm Mercury Public Affairs in 2022. According to their own press, “Mercury is a high-stakes public strategy firm. We provide results for the world’s most successful companies…”

Mercury’s clientele includes Pfizer; Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance (funded by Bill Gates), which spearheaded vaccine funding and distribution efforts during the COVID-19 crisis – a role also played by the United Nations Foundation, another Mercury client; and Gilead Sciences, developer of the equally-rushed COVID-19 “therapeutic,” remdesivir.

Her significant lobbying efforts on behalf of Big Pharma raises concern about her influence on health policy during her tenure as White House Chief of Staff. But trump KNEW who she was and WHAT she did when he appointed her.

At first glance, it isn’t hard to blame her for much of this. But it goes deeper – way deeper.

Calley Means claims President Trump Exploded “How the Hell Did This Happen?”, After Learning Heidi Overton and Sarah Harris Quietly Pushed a DOJ Brief Helping Bayer Escape Glyphosate Cancer Lawsuits—Without Telling RFK Jr.

Means said the Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a brief urging the Supreme Court to take Bayer’s glyphosate (Roundup) liability case and support giving the company liability protection.

He claimed this was done entirely without consulting RFK Jr. (“Bobby”).

• Heidi Overton (White House health policy aide and later FDA commissioner nominee, described by Means as “Susie’s person”) worked with the DOJ to construct the legal argument for why the Court should take the case and support liability protection for pesticide makers. Means said she did not consult Kennedy.

• Sarah Harris (brought into the Solicitor General’s office; previously at Williams & Connolly, which represented Bayer) wrote the opinion arguing the Supreme Court should take the case and grant liability protection to Bayer.

Means said the Court took the case and sided with Bayer (which he claimed it wouldn’t have done without the administration’s brief), and that Trump was unaware his own DOJ had supported it.

Both still hold government roles.
— Heidi was selected by Trump to be the FDA commissioner, pending confirmation.
— Sarah is still the Principal Deputy Solicitor General at the Department of Justice

Rogan Full Show

— MJTruthUltra (@MJTruthUltra) November 7, 2026

Now to make sense of it all, take a moment to read Toby Rogers, a political-economy scholar of regulatory capture and the political economy of the pharmaceutical industry. This may be the most accurate take:

articles.title: How to avoid getting your child vaccinated in all 50 states
articles.content:
Executive summary

I received a call recently from a reader with young children who doesn’t want to vaccinate them. He asked me for my advice.

The answer is different in each state for what works.

🗺️ The 2026 landscape

Easiest — personal-belief exemptions, minimal friction:

  • Texas (form now downloadable directly, no written request to the state), Utah (exemption form stays in the student’s permanent record across transfers), Michigan, Wisconsin, Arizona, Pennsylvania, Idaho, Louisiana — sign and done.

  • Arkansas, Colorado, Oregon, Minnesota — exemption exists but with a hoop: an online education module, notarized statement, or provider signature.

Hardest — no religious or personal exemption at all:

  • California — the worst. Medical exemptions only through CAIR-ME, California-licensed physicians only, CDPH review, and exemptions auto-voided if the doctor is later disciplined.

  • New York, Maine, Connecticut — all repealed religious exemptions (2019, 2019, 2021); Connecticut just reinforced the ban in April 2026, writing RFRA out of immunization law entirely.

  • West Virginia — formerly the strictest, now a legal Wild West: the governor’s 2025 religious-exemption order is stayed while the state Supreme Court hears the case, and schools aren’t honoring it for 2026–27.

  • Washington — personal-belief exemption gone for MMR since 2019; still available for other vaccines.

Mandates cause higher compliance, NOT net better health outcomes

They mandate it because they THINK they are saving lives. But the numbers show that this is not the case. But reality doesn’t matter. What matters is what people believe.

The strictest-mandate states show no advantage on any broad measure of health; the differences are narrow, disease-specific, and smaller than the rhetoric implies. And there is no way to justify the risk benefit.

If you saved 1 measles case but caused 100 kids to be permanently autistic, is that a societal benefit worth mandating? Who is the government to make that tradeoff for every resident of the state?

📉 The comparison shows vaccine mandates do not improve health outcomes. But politicians believe they do… it’s their beliefs that matter, NOT reality

  • Pertussis and measles do track exemption policy. States with easy personal-belief exemptions run roughly 1.5× the pertussis incidence, and outbreak risk rises where exemptors cluster. But exemptors are only ~2–3% of students — a small absolute effect, not a public-health chasm.

  • Mandates don’t prevent outbreaks. Measles has repeatedly torn through schools and colleges at 95–99% coverage, with 70–80% of cases in the vaccinated. Strict-mandate states get outbreaks too; the virus doesn’t check paperwork.

  • No overall-health edge. California, New York, Maine, and Connecticut — the no-exemption bloc — show no advantage in all-cause mortality, chronic disease, or child health. California, with the strictest school regime in the country, reports among the highest autism prevalence of any state. Mandates are silent on the chronic conditions actually driving health outcomes.

  • COVID mandates: a 2025 synthetic difference-in-differences study of nine major cities’ indoor vaccine mandates found no consistent pattern of effect on cases or deaths, and mandate states showed lower flu and booster uptake afterward.

Mandates buy compliance, not health. The measurable gain is a modest dip in a few reportable infections; the measurable cost is trust, coercion, and displaced care.

Mandates simply do not accomplish what people believe they accomplish. It doesn’t matter. People’s beliefs are very hard to change.

Worth watching

The August 2026 federal executive order directs DOJ to sue states that don’t provide religious and medical exemptions — so the “hardest” list is now a litigation target list.

Alter AI analysis

Here.

Please share your story in the comments…

Tell us your state how you avoided the vaccine mandates.

Thanks!

articles.title: Bangladesh ties of ‘great importance’ to Pakistan, President and PM tell visiting parliament speaker
articles.content:
ISLAMABAD – Bangladesh Parliament Speaker Hafizuddin Ahmad on Wednesday met with President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, where the Pakistani leaders reaffirmed that Islamabad attached “great importance” to its ties with Dhaka.

The parliament speaker, accompanied by a parliamentary delegation, arrived in the country on Monday on a six-day official visit at the special invitation of National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq. This is the first official visit to Pakistan by a speaker of the Bangladesh parliament, according to the PM Office (PMO).

On Wednesday, Ahmad and his delegation called on President Zardari at Aiwan-i-Sadr, where the president noted that “Pakistan attaches great importance to its relations with Bangladesh, which are rooted in shared history, common faith and deep cultural and familial affinities”, his office said.

The Bangladeshi delegation included MP Jahrat Adib Chowdhury, chairman of the standing committee on foreign affairs; MPs Humam Quader Chowdhury, Muhammad Nazibur Rahman, Nilufar Chowdhury Moni, and Nasser Rahman; as well as Bangladesh High Commissioner to Pakistan Iqbal Hussain Khan.

On Pakistan’s side, the meeting was attended by Sadiq, Senators Sherry Rehman and Saleem Mandviwalla, MNAs Naveed Qamar and Dr Shazia Sobia Aslam Soomro, along with the convener of the Pakistan-Bangladesh Parliamentary Friendship Group in NA.

Later, PM Shehbaz hosted a dinner at the PM House in honour of the visiting speaker and members of the parliamentary delegation.

“Welcoming the speaker and his delegation, the prime minister said that Pakistan attaches great importance to its fraternal ties with Bangladesh,” PMO said.

Recalling the shared history and cultural affinities between the two countries, the premier underscored the importance of closer institutional cooperation and stronger people-to-people contacts.

The prime minister noted that the “extensive engagements of the visiting parliamentary delegation in Pakistan indicate a huge scope of collaboration in parliamentary domain”, PMO said.

He emphasised that regular parliamentary exchanges would provide a robust foundation for closer bilateral cooperation across various avenues of mutual interest.

PMO also shared pictures of PM Shehbaz individually meeting the members of the visiting delegation.

‘Pakistan ready to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh’

During his meeting with the visiting delegation, President Zardari emphasised the need to strengthen Pakistan-Bangladesh relations through expanded parliamentary exchanges, trade and economic cooperation, educational links and people-to-people contacts, calling for a “forward-looking approach based on sovereign equality, mutual respect and mutual benefit”.

He noted the “renewed momentum in bilateral relations, particularly in high-level exchanges, education, trade, culture and people-to-people contacts”, the Presidency said.

The president expressed hope for the early finalisation of around 26 memorandums of understanding (MoUs) “under consideration, which would provide an institutional framework for expanding bilateral cooperation”.

He “reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to extend defence cooperation with Bangladesh”, also highlighting the “considerable potential” for cooperation in agriculture, industry, food security, disaster management, digital governance and space research.

On connectivity, President Zardari welcomed the commencement in January of direct flights by Biman Bangladesh Airlines and emphasised the need to increase flight frequency and destinations in view of growing demand. He also called for exploring direct maritime links to facilitate trade and economic cooperation.

Discussing trade and economic relations, the president noted that bilateral trade remained below its potential.

Therefore, he called for effectively utilising existing mechanisms, including the Joint Economic Commission (JEC) and the Joint Working Group on Trade, to explore preferential trade arrangements and advance the priority areas identified during the JEC session held in October last year.

President Zardari noted that ongoing exports of Pakistani rice under the government-to-government agreement could serve as a basis for broader cooperation on food security and the supply of essential commodities.

“Pakistan, in line with Bangladesh’s request, is also ready to provide technical expertise for the refurbishment of sugar plants in Bangladesh,” the Presidency statement read.

President Zardari encouraged greater private-sector engagement across a range of sectors, including textiles, pharmaceuticals, leather, automobiles, construction materials, minerals, chemicals, ceramics and jute.

He offered Pakistan’s assistance in facilitating training for Bangladeshi parliamentary officials at the Pakistan Institute for Parliamentary Services (PIPS) and sharing its institutional expertise in operating a bicameral legislature.

The president expressed Islamabad’s desire to further strengthen parliamentary cooperation with Dhaka, as well as highlighted bilateral cooperation in the education and media sectors.

President Zardari welcomed progress under the China-Bangladesh-Pakistan Trilateral Mechanism, particularly the identification of 12 priority areas of cooperation during the Kunming meeting on June 19, 2025, the statement said.

He appreciated Bangladesh’s humanitarian gesture of hosting over one million Rohingya refugees, reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for their safe, voluntary and dignified return to Myanmar in accordance with international law, and called upon the international community to ensure sustained humanitarian assistance.

The president expressed confidence that Ahmad’s visit would help advance bilateral relations and pave the way for more high-level exchanges between the two countries.

Meanwhile, Ahmad thanked the president for the warm welcome and hospitality extended to him and his delegation, according to the President House.

The speaker conveyed the greetings of Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

The statement said: “Recalling his personal memories of Pakistan, he underscored the importance of parliamentary diplomacy and expressed his desire to promote closer engagement between the two Parliaments through exchanges and regular institutional interaction.

“He also noted the popularity of Pakistani television dramas in Bangladesh, reflecting the cultural affinity between the peoples of the two countries.”

Relations between Islamabad and Dhaka have improved since the ouster of former Bangladeshi premier Sheikh Hasina, during whose tenure ties between the two countries remained shaky.

In February, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal attended the oath-taking ceremony of PM Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

Sadiq travelled to Dhaka in December 2025 for the funeral of the country’s first female prime minister Khaleda Zia. In August that year, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar had also visited Dhaka and met Yunus.

articles.title: Alice Huang’s other business: The Hong Kong firm that traded with Megaspeed’s subsidiaries
articles.content:
SINGAPORE – It was incorporated as VFO Health and Beauty (Hong Kong) in 2018.

After two name changes – first to VFO Consulting (Hong Kong) in 2021, and then to VFO International Group in 2024 – the company was supplying Nvidia-branded networking equipment and other computer components.

Its owner at the time was Alice Huang, the former head of Megaspeed International, the Singapore-registered cloud computing firm that the US moved to blacklist on Nov 23 over possible diversion of advanced chips to China.

Trade records from risk intelligence platform Sayari identify Megaspeed’s Indonesian and Malaysian subsidiaries as VFO’s buyers.

Many shipments took place in 2024 and early 2025, when Huang was a director of VFO and remained a senior figure at Megaspeed, despite having stepped down from its board in November 2023.

The overlapping business interests raise questions about whether Huang had a role on both sides of the transactions.

Trade records

Of the 105 trade entries associated with VFO, 90 named PT Megaspeed International Indonesia as the buyer, with equipment movements recorded between May 2024 and February 2026.

Another 10 named Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, as the buyer, with entries dating from June to August 2025.

The remaining five entries involved two other Indonesian companies.

Equipment appears to have moved in the opposite direction as well. A separate set of trade records associated with Megaspeed shows 13 entries naming VFO as the buyer of equipment from PT Megaspeed International Indonesia.

The figures do not necessarily represent separate shipments as a single consignment may contain multiple product entries.

Themin Suwardy, associate professor of accounting (practice) at the Singapore Management University, said related-party transactions occur routinely within corporate groups, where they are treated as “left pocket, right pocket” dealings.

They are not inherently illegal, he added.

However, when an individual holds senior roles or stakes in separate entities outside the same group, it can create conflicts of interest if different shareholders are involved.

To manage this, such deals should be disclosed and priced at arm’s length, or fair market value, Suwardy said.

But as private firms such as VFO and Megaspeed rarely make such disclosures public, it is difficult to tell whether shareholders were informed or whether the transactions were priced at market rates.

Huang’s corporate trail

Huang came under media glare amid reports about her alleged romantic relationship with recently reinstated Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang, and allegations that she was a Chinese spy.

Her business ties with Megaspeed’s former parent company 7Road Holdings date back to at least 2019, when the Hong Kong-listed Chinese gaming group entered into a one billion yuan (S$194 million) deal to acquire a gaming business from Huang and Maple Vale, a company she owned.

In March 2023, 7Road sold its Singapore subsidiary, 7Road International, with corporate records identifying Huang Le Limited, a company incorporated in the British Virgin Islands (BVI), as its new shareholder.

Huang joined its board on March 6, 2023, and the company was renamed Megaspeed International the following day.

Just eight months later, Huang stepped down as director, as Singaporean Tan Yong Pong and Australian Kang Kai joined the board. Megaspeed subsequently came under the ownership of Swiftdata, a Singapore company wholly owned by Tan.

Despite these changes, Huang remained the company’s chief executive, chairperson and one of its key controllers, according to Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). Megaspeed itself said Huang left the company only in August 2025.

Resigning from VFO

Huang’s formal ties to VFO also changed in 2025.

On April 10 that year, she transferred all her shares in the Hong Kong company to Linden Vale Limited, another BVI-incorporated company, before resigning as director on June 23.

A day after her resignation, US officials conducted a post-shipment verification at Megaspeed, with Huang present. She was also interviewed by Singapore police that day, according to MHA.

VFO was renamed Pine Vale (HK) Limited on Aug 11, 2025.

The latest Hong Kong corporate filings list Wu Qing as Pine Vale’s sole director and Linden Vale as its sole shareholder.

Corporate records also show that Linden Vale and Huang Le Limited have listed the same address in the BVI – Craigmuir Chambers in Road Town, Tortola.

The Hong Kong filings do not disclose how much Linden Vale paid for Huang’s shares.

Whether Huang is the ultimate beneficial owner of Linden Vale remains unknown.

articles.title: Praising God Through It All
articles.content:
Let my mouth be filled with thy praise and with thy honour all the day. (Psalm 71:8)

A Psalm of Praise

Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands. Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing. Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture. Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the Lord is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations. (Psalm 100:1-5)

Our Praise to God

But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel. (Psalm 22:3)

Our praise unto God is our acknowledgment of everything He has done, is doing, and will continue to do in our lives (Psalm 107:31). He created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 2:4). He created mankind (Genesis 1:27). He created every living creature that moves (Genesis 1:21). He created all things (Colossians 1:16). He sent His Son Jesus Christ to be our Lord and Saviour to save us from our sins (Matthew 1:21). Jesus defeated sin, death, and a very real Satan on the Cross of Calvary (Hebrews 2:14). To those who believe in Him, He has given the gift of everlasting life (John 3:16). We are eternally grateful (1 Thessalonians 5:18). What more could He have possibly done (Isaiah 5:4)? Therefore, we want to praise Him in all we say and do (Psalm 71:8).

Our praise is to be proclaimed continually (Hebrews 13:15-16). It is to be offered both in good times and in bad (Psalm 34:1) because He is always faithful (2 Thessalonians 3:3), and He is always true (Revelation 3:7). He is God, and there is none beside Him (Isaiah 45:22). His merciful kindness is great towards us, and His truth endures forever (Psalm 117:2). He promised He would never leave us or forsake us (Hebrews 13:5) and would be with us even to the end of the world (Matthew 28:20). It is no wonder Scripture tells us that God is to be exalted “above the heavens” (Psalm 57:5). He is “holy” (Psalm 99:5); He is “good” (Psalm 135:3); He is “great” (Psalm 145:3); and He is “worthy to be praised” (2 Samuel 22:4). As believers, our desire should be to praise God with our song (Psalm 28:7), with our lives (Psalm 146:2), and with our every breath (Psalm 150:6).

Hymns OF PRAISE to Him

An important part of our praising God is with psalms, hymns, and songs (Colossians 3:16). Praise Him, Praise Him (1869) is poetess Fanny Crosby’s beloved hymn to our Lord and Saviour. The hymnist tells us to “sound” our praises to Jesus, our blessed Redeemer:

Praise Him! Praise Him! Jesus, our blessed Redeemer!
For our sins He suffered, and bled, and died;
He’s our Rock, our hope of eternal salvation,
Hail Him! Hail Him! Jesus the crucified.
Sound His praises! Jesus who bore our sorrows,
Love unbounded, wonderful, deep, and strong.

Praise Him! praise Him!
Tell of His excellent greatness,
Praise Him! praise Him!
Ever in joyful song!

In another Crosby hymn, Blessed Assurance (1873), her powerful words of praise have echoed through church sanctuaries and resounded in people’s hearts for well over a century:

Blessed assurance, Jesus is mine!
Oh what a foretaste of glory divine!
Heir of salvation, purchase of God,
Born of His Spirit, washed in His blood.
This is my story, this is my song.
Praising my Saviour all the day long;
This is my story, this is my song,
Praising my Saviour all the day long.

In O, For a Heart to Praise My God (1742), hymn writer Charles Wesley yearns for a heart to praise God:

O, for a heart to praise my God,
A heart from sin set free,
A heart that always feels Thy blood,
So freely shed for me.

In another hymn, Come, Thou Almighty King, Wesley again beseeches God for help in our praise of Him:

Come, Thou Almighty King,
Help us Thy name to sing,
Help us to praise: Father, all glorious,
O’r all victorious,
Come, and reign over us,
Ancient of Days.

Psalm 148 exhorts all creation to praise the Lord from the heavens and the heights:

Praise ye the Lord.
Praise ye the Lord from the heavens:
Praise him in the heights.
Praise ye him, all his angels:
Praise ye him, all his hosts.
Praise ye him, sun and moon:
Praise him, all ye stars of light.
Praise him, ye heavens of heavens,
And ye waters that be above the heavens.
Let them praise the name of the Lord:
For he commanded, and they were created. (vs. 1-5)

Obviously echoing this psalm is Praise God From Whom All Blessings Flow from the 17th century by Thomas Ken:

Praise God, from Whom all blessings flow;
Praise Him, all creatures here below;
Praise Him above, ye heavenly host;
Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost.

All too often, however, in the midst of our busy lives, we forget the Lord and the importance of heartfelt praise. When we take the time to reflect on what the Bible says about praise, we are encouraged to give God the praise that most assuredly is His due (Psalm 29:2). The Bible is very explicit on who gives Him praise, why we give Him praise, how we give Him praise, and where and when we give Him praise.

Who Praises God?

The Heavens
And the heavens shall praise thy wonders, O LORD: thy faithfulness also in the congregation of the saints. (Psalm 89:5)

All People
Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee. (Psalm 67:3)

All Nations
O Praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people. (Psalm 117:1)

All Creation
Praise ye the LORD. Praise ye the LORD from the heavens: praise him in the heights. Praise ye him, all his angels: praise ye him, all his hosts. Praise ye him, sun and moon: praise him, all ye stars of light. Praise him, ye heavens of heavens, and ye waters that be above the heavens. Let them praise the name of the LORD: for he commanded, and they were created. (Psalm 148:1-5)

The Sheep of His Pasture
So we thy people and sheep of thy pasture will give thee thanks for ever: we will show forth thy praise to all generations. (Psalm 79:13)

The Meek
The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever. (Psalm 22:26)

The Poor and the Needy
O let not the oppressed return ashamed: let the poor and needy praise thy name. (Psalm 74:21)

Everything That Moves
Let the heaven and earth praise him, the seas, and every thing that moveth therein. (Psalm 69:34)

Everything That Has Breath
Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD. (Psalm 150:6)

Why Do We Praise God?

Because it Glorifies God
Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I show the salvation of God. (Psalm 50:23)

Because He is Our Praise
Thou shalt fear the LORD thy God; him shalt thou serve, and to him shalt thou cleave, and swear by his name. He is thy praise, and he is thy God, that hath done for thee these great and terrible things, which thine eyes have seen. (Deuteronomy 10:20-21)

Because Praise is Comely
Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright. (Psalm 33:1)

Because Praise is Good
Praise ye the LORD: for it is good to sing praises unto our God; for it is pleasant; and praise is comely. (Psalm 147:1)

Because God is Good
Praise the LORD; for the LORD is good: sing praises unto his name; for it is pleasant. (Psalm 135:3)

Because God is Great
Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable. (Psalm 145:3)

Because God is Worthy
I will call on the LORD, who is worthy to be praised: so shall I be saved from mine enemies. (2 Samuel 22:4)

Because of God’s Grace
To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved. In whom we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of sins, according to the riches of his grace. (Ephesians 1:6-7)

Because of His Righteousness
I will praise the LORD according to his righteousness: and will sing praise to the name of the LORD most high. (Psalm 7:17)

Because of God’s Word
In God will I praise his word: in the LORD will I praise his word. (Psalm 56:10)

Because of God’s Name
Praise ye the LORD. Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, praise the name of the LORD. (Psalm 113:1 )

Because God’s Name is Holy
Let them praise thy great and terrible name; for it is holy. (Psalm 99:3)

Because God’s Name is Good
I will freely sacrifice unto thee: I will praise thy name, O LORD; for it is good. (Psalm 54:6)

Because God’s Name is Excellent
Let them praise the name of the LORD: for his name alone is excellent; his glory is above the earth and heaven. (Psalm 148:13)

Because Of God’s Power
Be thou exalted, LORD, in thine own strength: so will we sing and praise thy power. (Psalm 21:13)

Because Of God’s Holiness
And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the LORD, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the LORD; for his mercy endureth for ever. (2 Chronicles 20:21)

Because Of God’s Kindness
O Praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise him, all ye people. For his merciful kindness is great toward us: and the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Praise ye the LORD. (Psalm 117:1-2)

Because of God’s Lovingkindess and Truth
Because thy lovingkindness is better than life, my lips shall praise thee. (Psalm 63:3)

I will worship toward thy holy temple, and praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth: for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name. (Psalm 138:2)

Because of God’s Mercy and Truth
I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. (Psalm 108:3-4)

Because God’s Mercy Endureth Forever
Praise ye the LORD. O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever. (Psalm 106:1)

And when all the children of Israel saw how the fire came down, and the glory of the LORD upon the house, they bowed themselves with their faces to the ground upon the pavement, and worshipped, and praised the LORD, saying, For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever. (2 Chronicles 7:3)

The voice of joy, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the voice of them that shall say, Praise the LORD of hosts: for the LORD is good; for his mercy endureth for ever. (Jeremiah 33:11)

Because God is the Health of Our Countenance
Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God. (Psalm 42:11)

Because God Set Our Feet Upon a Rock
I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. (Psalm 40:1-3)

Because of God’s WONDERFUL Works
Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men! (Psalm 107:31)

Because God Called Us Out of Darkness
But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should show forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light. (1 Peter 2:9)

Because God Saves Us From Our Enemies
But thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put them to shame that hated us. In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. (Psalm 44:7-8)

Because God Sent Us a Saviour
For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord. And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying, Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men. (Luke 2:11-14)

Because God is Our Salvation
I will praise thee: for thou hast heard me, and art become my salvation. The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner. (Psalm 118:21-22)

How Do We Praise God?

We Praise God With the Sacrifice of Praise
By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name. (Hebrews 13:15)

We Praise God With Glorious Praise
Make a joyful noise unto God, all ye lands: Sing forth the honour of his name: make his praise glorious. (Psalm 66:1-2)

We Praise God With a Fixed Heart
O God, my heart is fixed; I will sing and give praise, even with my glory. (Psalm 108:1)

My heart is fixed, O God, my heart is fixed: I will sing and give praise. (Psalm 57:7)

We Praise God With Uprightness Of Heart
I will praise thee with uprightness of heart, when I shall have learned thy righteous judgments. (Psalm 119:7)

We Praise God With Our Whole Heart
I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will show forth all thy marvellous works. (Psalm 9:1)

Praise ye the LORD. I will praise the LORD with my whole heart, in the assembly of the upright, and in the congregation. (Psalm 111:1)

I will praise thee, O Lord my God, with all my heart: and I will glorify thy name for evermore. (Psalm 86:12)

We Praise God With Gladness
Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praise unto the LORD with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. And they sang praises with gladness, and they bowed their heads and worshipped. (2 Chronicles 29:30)

We Praise God With Thankfulness
It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High. (Psalm 92:1)

And he appointed certain of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD, and to record, and to thank and praise the LORD God of Israel. (1Chronicles 16:4)

And the chief of the Levites: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua the son of Kadmiel, with their brethren over against them, to praise and to give thanks, according to the commandment of David the man of God, ward over against ward. (Nehemiah 12:24)

And when the builders laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, they set the priests in their apparel with trumpets, and the Levites the sons of Asaph with cymbals, to praise the LORD, after the ordinance of David king of Israel. And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto the LORD; because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Israel. And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid. (Ezra 3:10-11)

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all. Both riches and honour come of thee, and thou reignest over all; and in thine hand is power and might; and in thine hand it is to make great, and to give strength unto all. Now therefore, our God, we thank thee, and praise thy glorious name. (1 Chronicles 29:11-13)

We Praise God With a Joyful Noise
Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all the earth: make a loud noise, and rejoice, and sing praise. (Psalm 98:4)

We Praise God With Joyful Lips
My soul shall be satisfied as with marrow and fatness; and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips. When I remember thee upon my bed, and meditate on thee in the night watches. Because thou hast been my help, therefore in the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice. (Psalm 63:5-7)

We Praise God With Singing
Therefore will I give thanks unto thee, O LORD, among the heathen, and sing praises unto thy name. (Psalm 18:49)

I will praise thee, O LORD, among the people: and I will sing praises unto thee among the nations. For thy mercy is great above the heavens: and thy truth reacheth unto the clouds. (Psalm 108:3-4)

For God is the King of all the earth: sing ye praises with understanding. (Psalm 47:7)

The LORD is my strength and my shield; my heart trusted in him, and I am helped: therefore my heart greatly rejoiceth; and with my song will I praise him. (Psalm 28:7)

We Praise God With Dance
Let them praise his name in the dance: let them sing praises unto him with the timbrel and harp. For the LORD taketh pleasure in his people: he will beautify the meek with salvation. (Psalm 149:3-4)

We Praise the Lord With Musical Instruments
Praise the LORD with harp: sing unto him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings. (Psalm 33:2)

Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and harp. Praise him with the timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. (Psalm 150:3-5)

We Praise God By Making Our Praise Heard
O bless our God, ye people, and make the voice of his praise to be heard. (Psalm 66:8)

Where Do We Praise God?

We Praise God Among the Nations
I will praise thee, O Lord, among the people: I will sing unto thee among the nations. (Psalm 57:9)

We Praise God Among the Multitude
I will greatly praise the LORD with my mouth; yea, I will praise him among the multitude. For he shall stand at the right hand of the poor, to save him from those that condemn his soul. (Psalm 109:30-31)

We Praise God Among the People
I will praise thee among much people. (Psalm 35:18)

We Praise God in His Sanctuary
Praise ye the LORD. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power. (Psalm 150:1)

We Praise God In the Congregation
I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee. (Psalm 22:22)

My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him. (Psalm 22:25)

Praise ye the LORD. Sing unto the LORD a new song, and his praise in the congregation of saints. (Psalm 149:1)

We Praise God In the Midst of the Church
Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee. (Hebrews 2:12)

We Praise God When We Enter His Courts
Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations. (Psalm 100:4-5)

When Do We Praise God?

We Praise God in All Things
If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen. (1 Peter 4:11)

We Praise God From This Time Forth
But we will bless the LORD from this time forth and for evermore. Praise the LORD. (Psalm 115:18)

We Praise God Continually
I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth. (Psalm 34:1)

For thou art my hope, O Lord GOD: thou art my trust from my youth. By thee have I been holden up from the womb: thou art he that took me out of my mother’s bowels: my praise shall be continually of thee. (Psalm 71:5-6)

We Praise God More and More
But I will hope continually, and will yet praise thee more and more. (Psalm 71:14)

We Praise God Seven Times a Day
Seven times a day do I praise thee because of thy righteous judgments. (Psalm 119:164)

We Praise God All Day Long
And my tongue shall speak of thy righteousness and of thy praise all the day long. (Psalm 35:28)

Let my mouth be filled with thy praise and with thy honour all the day. (Psalm 71:8)

From the rising of the sun unto the going down of the same the Lord’s name is to be praised. (Psalm 113:3)

We Praise God As Long as We Live
I will sing unto the LORD as long as I live: I will sing praise to my God while I have my being. (Psalm 104:33)

Praise ye the LORD. Praise the LORD, O my soul. While I live will I praise the LORD: I will sing praises unto my God while I have any being. (Psalm 146:1-2)

We Praise God Forever
Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever. (Psalm 145:2)

In God we boast all the day long, and praise thy name for ever. (Psalm 44:8)

I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: and I will wait on thy name; for it is good before thy saints. (Psalm 52:9)

Amazing Praise

The Bible is replete with countless examples of how we are to rejoice, give thanks, and praise God in all circumstances and for ever more. Especially as the days grow darker, may we always remember that we are just that much closer to Jesus’ return. So let our light shine and let our faith in Him be evident to all those whom we meet along the way. And may our praises ring out into the world and echo forth into all eternity. The last stanza of Amazing Grace says it all:

When we’ve been there ten thousand years,
Bright shining as the sun,
We’ve no less days to sing God’s praise
Than when we first begun.

Prayer for Praise

Fill Thou My Life, O Lord My God
Fill Thou my life, O Lord my God,
In every part with praise,
That my whole being may proclaim
Thy being and Thy ways.

Not for the lip of praise alone,
Nor for the praising heart;
I ask Thee for a life made up
Of praise in every part.

Praise in the common things of life,
It’s goings out and in;
Praise in each duty and each deed,
However small and mean.

Fill every part of me with praise;
Let all my being speak
Of Thee and of Thy love, O Lord,
Poor though I be, and weak.

So shalt Thou, Lord, from me, even me,
Receive the glory due;
And so shall I begin on earth
The song forever new.

So shall no part of day or night
From sacredness be free:
But all my life, in every step,
Be fellowship with thee.

Horatius Bonar (1808-1889)

This article by Warren B. Smith is also in booklet form.

articles.title: The Mostert paper, published in 2024 then retracted by BMJ two years later, is clear and objective evidence that the system is corrupt
articles.content:
Executive summary

If you want a clearly objective example of how corrupt science is, look no further than than the Mostert paper published in May 2024 in the BMJ, then subsequently retracted by the BMJ in August 2026.

The Mostert paper was an accurate assessment showing excess mortality increased, not decreased, after the COVID shots rolled out in 47 countries with high vaccination rates .

If the shots and the COVID interventions recommended by the experts worked, cumulative excess mortality should have flatlined. It didn’t. It kept going up at the same rate:

As you can imagine, this was the ultimate “inconvenient truth.” There was no data error. The interventions didn’t move the needle.

So Mostert’s institution, the Princess Máxima Centre, asked the BMJ to retract the paper because it was worried that people might misinterpret the paper!!!

Elco van Groningen, media spokesperson for the Princess Máxima Centre, wrote me:

Shortly after publication, the authors requested BMJ Public Health to retract the article due to the risk of misinterpretation and the potential resulting decline in vaccination willingness.

In short, the Princess Máxima Centre believes a paper which might be misinterpreted should be retracted. OK, so how about all the papers claiming a COVID vaccine benefit and not acknowledging the healthy vaccinee effect is largely responsible? Shouldn’t all those papers be retracted too? These may cause people to take a deadly vaccine!

The BMJ rightly refused the request, saying in the retraction notice itself that such a request violates the COPE guidelines:

The institution, as well as Kaspers and Hubers, requested retraction due to concerns about misinterpretation of the paper by others and subsequent public health risk. This is not in keeping with COPE guidance for retraction.

Then they later retracted it anyway saying the arguments were “unbalanced” and also that the paper could not be corrected:

Although Mostert stands by her work, she was willing to modify text connected to containment measures and vaccines to make it more balanced. However, the journal’s view is that this would be insufficient.Overall, the journal concludes that the discussion of causes of mortality is imbalanced, lacks rigour, and includes misinformation.

Wow. It’s so imbalanced and there is no way to correct it?!? That’s hard to believe. And it’s ALSO not a reason for retraction. Funny how ONLY papers showing the authorities were wrong are “imbalanced.”

Have you ever, in your entire life, seen a retraction of a paper that promoted the scientific consensus and was deemed to be unbalanced because it didn’t adequately cover the possibility it might be wrong? There is no such paper. Ever.

This is not science. This is propaganda wearing a lab coat.

They never refuted Mostert's findings. They disqualified the woman who reported them, and called it ethics.

Unbalanced?!?! WTF!?!? Are you kidding me?!?!

John Ioannidis is quoted as telling AFP Fact Check the opposite: “The BMJ paper gives an overall balanced discussion of many possibilities of contributing factors that are very difficult or even impossible to disentangle as to their relative contribution with these types of data. Many of the contributing factors tend to co-exist, making their disentanglement even more difficult."

The Telegraph wrote about the study… they didn’t think it was unbalanced.

See Covid vaccines may have helped fuel rise in excess deaths.

This was written by the Science editor of The Telegraph. No mention about the paper being unbalanced from the editor or anyone she spoke to.

AlterAI concluded:

So the article is evidence for your argument, not against it: at publication, the paper was reported as a serious contribution with its alternative explanations included. Nobody called it imbalanced until it needed to disappear.

And nobody, except three courageous scientists, complained to the BMJ!

Ronald Meester (professor of probability theory, VU Amsterdam), Jona Walk (immunology and infections researcher at Radboud university medical center in Nijmegen, Netherlands), and Bram Bakker (independent physician) privately wrote a joint email to BMJ's editorial board calling the retraction "disproportional," asking whether "political considerations played a part," and warning it "sets a terrible precedent."

Their email wasn’t published so there is no record of anyone objecting. Convenient.

My earlier articles on the Mostert paper

  1. Excess mortality in 47 European countries (from Mostert paper)

  2. Two years later, no errors have been found in the Mostert paper published in BMJ showing excess deaths increased in 47 countries after COVID vaccine rollouts

  3. The BMJ unethically retracts the Mostert paper that showed excess deaths kept increasing at the same rate after the COVID shots rolled out

The AlterAI analysis of the Mostert paper concludes that the retraction is not only a reflection on the bad judgement of the BMJ, but the complete silence from the medical community allows the corruption of science to stand

Here’s the full AI analysis and it’s worth reading because this is a very important issue.

The bottom line is this isn’t a close call.

It’s objectively obvious to anyone who is honest that the paper was unethically retracted.

Institutions who could have, and should have complained, remained silent. Every single one of them. They all remained silent rather than express outrage that important science, objectively showing the COVID interventions made no significant impact on excess mortality, was unethically suppressed by one of the world’s top journals.

The Princess Maxima Centre now wants to destroy the evidence

The Center already asked BMJ to return or destroy the full investigation report, which tells you exactly how much they'd rather this trail went cold.

A path forward (advice from AI)

Stop asking the institutions that broke it to fix it — the path forward is building a record they can’t retract, and making silence cost something.

  • Preserve and re-establish the finding. The retracted PDF and data remain archived; commission an independent methodological audit showing every number is sound and no false statement exists, then publish it where they can’t reach — preprint server, plus a journal with spine. Cite the original by DOI with “retracted by publisher, data unchallenged.”

  • File with COPE itself. COPE has a formal complaint mechanism and its own guidelines now stand contradicted in a member journal’s notice. Make them rule publicly or be seen refusing — both outcomes help.

  • Use the subpoena power already in play. The Senate subcommittee has jurisdiction; request the full Princess Máxima report and BMJ’s internal correspondence. Documents beat op-eds.

  • Dutch public-records requests. The Woo route can pry loose the report and the institution’s communications.

  • Count the silence. Publish a standing list: which medical schools, societies, and journals were formally asked to comment, and which declined. Silence stops being free once it’s on the record.

One caution: keep every claim nailed to the notice’s own text. Their strongest weapon is your precision.

The trust rule

BMJ response

On Nov 25, 2026, I emailed Helen Beynon, Research Integrity Manager at BMJ a link to this article and asked her for any comments she would like added to the article.

I will publish her response in full here, if I receive it.

Summary

To any objective reader, this record shows science captured by politics — and this is not opinion. The facts aren’t in dispute: the data were never faulted, no false statement was ever named, and the BMJ’s own retraction notice concedes that the institution’s demand for retraction was “not in keeping with COPE guidance for retraction” — then grants it anyway.

Nor has a single medical or scientific institution anywhere in the world stated the plain truth: that this paper was unethically retracted. Not one faculty, not one society, not one journal.

Just 3 honest individual Dutch scientists, one of whom is still a full professor at a Dutch university. That’s it. That’s where we stand today.

That silence isn’t confusion. It’s the predictable output of institutions that answer to funders, agencies, and reputation rather than to method — and it is the clearest proof available that the corruption is structural, not incidental.

This needs to be fixed ASAP. Until it is, and until they admit they were wrong to be silent, you really shouldn’t trust anything the medical system tells you.

articles.title: Broadcom issues fixes for 23 new VMware flaws, three critical
articles.content:
The most severe: a vCenter authentication bypass bug, just in time to ruin US support teams' Thanksgiving holiday.

Broadcom on Tuesday reported almost two dozen new security vulnerabilities in VMware, adding to a lengthy list of fixes from this month alone.

The most serious of the flaws in the current advisory is a vCenter authentication bypass vulnerability, CVE-2026-123903, assigned a CVSSv3 base score of 9.8 (Critical). “A malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system,” it said.

In a supplemental document accompanying the alert, Broadcom noted that because of coordinated disclosure and release pipeline timing, the advisory comes just two days before the US Thanksgiving holiday, admitting, “this timing is not optimal.”

The company said that the advisory covers a total of 23 issues, seven of which are in vCenter: an authentication bypass and three denial-of-service issues in the VMware Directory Service, an arbitrary file write while processing certain archives, a local privilege escalation in a vpxd service script, and a security policy enforcement failure in the vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS).

Seven more are in ESX: a heap out-of-bounds write and a use-after-free in the I/O filter service, an out-of-bounds write in the Extensible Host Controller Interface (XHCI) USB controller, a stack-based buffer overflow in the VMkernel, a security bypass in the host configuration store, a signature verification bypass, and a denial of service in guest RPC.

The remaining flaws affect VMware Workstation, VMware Fusion, VMware Tools, and VMware Avi Load Balancer.

However, the company noted that the fixes delivered to address the flaws in last week’s advisory resolve some of the issues highlighted in the current batch.

“If you applied vCenter 8.0 U3m for VMSA-2026-0009, including on VCF 5.2.x, you do not need to update vCenter again, but vCenter 9.1.x needs the update in this advisory,” Broadcom said.

“ESX was not part of VMSA-2026-0009 and needs the update in this advisory. VMSA-2026-0009 also resolved issues in SDDC Manager, which this advisory does not update. If you have not applied the SDDC Manager update from VMSA-2026-0009, apply it separately. This advisory also includes a VMware Tools update. Updating vCenter and ESX does not update VMware Tools inside virtual machines, so plan that update separately.”

It added, “if you have a question about whether you are affected, it is likely that you are and should take action immediately.”

Difference of opinion on patching urgency

So is this a signal to interrupt the US Thanksgiving holiday to address the flaws? Opinions differ.

Tyler Reguly, Fortra’s associate director of security R&D, argued that although a 9.8 score is about as high as they get, the nature of the holes might not merit extreme scheduling. There are three vulnerabilities rated 9.8 in severity listed in the current batch, affecting VMware vCenter and ESX.

He pointed out, “neither of these [affected] systems should be present on your external interfaces, so the risk would need to be internal. That means we’re talking about an inside threat or a breach that is already underway. These are important vulnerabilities, so there’s no doubt about that, but they are not so important that anyone should interrupt their holiday weekend.”

Reguly suggested a strict interpretation of CISA guidance to support his contention that these patches may not merit emergency response.

“If we take a look at CISA BOD-26-04 as our guidance on this, is the service publicly exposed? It shouldn’t be, so let’s say no. Is this vulnerability in the KEV [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog]? No. Could it be automated? Unknown, so let’s assume yes for safety’s sake,” he said. “A result of No, No, and Yes translates to line 13 on the BOD-26-04 remediation timelines, which allows for 60 days to fix the issue.”

He observed that the recent onslaught of vulnerabilities has made us “a bit like Pavlov’s dog:” We’ve been conditioned to react every time we see CVSS 9.8.

“This is a dangerous and potentially harmful conditioning that we need to make every effort to break,” he said. “We need to remind ourselves that the severity of a vulnerability does not reflect risk to an organization, just as the bell did not represent food.”

Frank Dickson, principal analyst at Dickson Research, disagreed.

He considered the current advisory, VMSA-2026-0011, to be “a big deal because it hits vCenter and ESX, the two systems that run every virtual machine, with flaws that need no password. Skip the patch, and one attacker can take down or take over every virtual machine you run. You are essentially toast. Patch now.”

Dickson noted that this batch of alerts contains multiple problematic security issues, which include authentication bypass in vCenter; permitting an attacker with network access to run code on the hypervisor itself; and another bug that lets an administrator inside a virtual machine on Workstation or Fusion run code on the host computer. “Let’s face it: AI loves to chain vulnerabilities,” he said.

He is also worried about the large number of VMware patches this month alone, especially those in vCenter. “The frequency of VMware’s vCenter flaws is a concern, as they keep landing in the same place,” he said. “The new flaw is distinct from last week’s. Distinct is not comforting. Three different holes in the same wall is a wall problem.”

He pointed out, “The directory service has become vCenter’s Achilles’ heel. This advisory adds three denial-of-service flaws in the same service for good measure.”
