articles.title: Forming a Universal Truth Movement – Part 2
articles.content:
Forming a Universal Truth Movement – Part 2

In Part 1 we considered the attributes of successful movements and determined that there is currently no functioning Truth Movement (TM).

We defined the Establishment and recognised that challenging the Establishment’s status quo, to some greater or lesser extent, is what movements do. Successful movements build on campaign successes and offer compelling narratives that build social momentum to deliver their long-term vision.

At their best, a movement’s long-term vision remedies the identified Establishment problem[s], whatever the exposed problem[s] may be.

In the previous article we noted that there are already a number of different anti-Establishment truths that prospective “T-Mers”—potential members of our envisaged Truth Movement (TM)—are actively pursuing: 9/11 was a false flag, climate alarm is a scam, Covid was a psyop, the digital transformation is the path to Technocracy, etc.

If, however, the hope is to form a united sociopolitical movement that, as its prospective name suggests, bases its campaigns on a fundamental “truth,” that truth has to unify all T-Mers. The alternative is to insist that every T-Mer agrees on a growing list of of truth related topics.

As each of the aforementioned examples of areas of research—9/11, climate change, Covid, etc.—elicit a range of often opposing views, our hoped-for TM runs the risk of never agreeing anything.

To reiterate a point made in Part 1, there is no problem with disagreement. A notable strength of successful movements is their ability to manage internal disputes without falling apart. Cohesion is maintained because, despite their differences, the movement’s long-term vision is one that all movement members not only share but truly believe in. Successful movements are formed by people willing to relentlessly pursue that vision, perhaps at considerable personal cost. A halfhearted movement is no more than a pointless gesture.

Let’s consider what that potential unifying T-Mer truth might be, or at least contemplate its possible foundation. I recently read a comment on my Telegram channel from a potential T-Mer who bemoaned the fact that 25 years after 9/11, with all the ensuing illegal wars, toxic poisoning, the Epstein revelations, and more, the Truth Movement had achieved precisely nothing. His frustration is perhaps something we all share, though placing any faith in a nonexistent TM doesn’t help.

Slightly contrary to this somewhat depressing realisation, the disparate bands of 9/11, Covid, climate, anti-war and other “truthers” have, in fact, achieved something quite significant. We’ll get to that in a moment.

The Light paper—a good candidate for a T-Mer news outlet—observed that we are all “under attack from the most violent, terrorist, extremist, psychopathic scum there has ever been.” Therefore, the Light continued, “we need to double or triple our efforts (or get started) and stop thinking it will all go away” and “take part in active resistance wherever possible and legal (because they want to be able to incarcerate you too.)”

We do indeed need to get started with active lawful and peaceable resistance—we’ll further clarify why our hopeful TM has to be lawful and peaceable in Part 3. That said, what kind of active resistance can we start and to what ends?

With those questions in mind, as I previously mentioned, I was delighted to meet a great bunch at the recent Real Left conference. Among them was Rusere Shoniwa, whose thought provoking work can be found at A Plague on Both Houses. Shoniwa has offered a reasonable list of the kind of things he sees a TM standing against:

Anti-imperialist; anti-colonialist; anti-System; anti-Establishment; anti New World Order; anti-Multipolar World Order; anti-UN; anti-Sustainability agenda; anti-Zionist; anti-Covidian; anti-Pandemic ‘awareness’; anti-medical coercion of any kind; anti-Left/Right Punch and Judy show; anti-Climate Alarmism; anti-Geoengineering; anti Digital ID; anti-CBDCs and all crypto currencies; anti-AI; anti-Fourth Industrial Revolution; anti-all political parties and anti-voting.

You might not agree with all of these potential points of TM opposition but that doesn’t matter—bear with me for now. If we consider the comments on my Telegram channel, the Light paper’s observations and Shoniwa’s list, I suggest a possible T-Mer common cause, or underlying truth, is identifiable.

I preface the rest of this essay (continued in Part 3) by stating my belief in objective morality. In my view there are seven objectively immoral acts: murder, rape, assault, theft, trespass, deception, and coercion. It is morally wrong to commit any of these acts no matter who you are and regardless of which group or organisation you represent.

Shoniwa lists some of the Establishment’s immoral acts. The use of force to commit murder, rape, and assault (imperialism, colonialism, and neocolonialism), the Establishment’s use of force to commit trespass (Covidian lockdowns, geoengineering), and the Establishment’s use of force to deceive and coerce (climate propaganda spread by legally protected media outlets and academia while counter-arguments are censored, the imposition of digital ID linked to programmable digital currencies to control our behaviour). All are examples of objectively immoral acts and all stem from the Establishment’s use or intended use of its hypothetical supreme authority.

Both The Light and my Telegram Channel commenter stress that the Establishment commits these objectively immoral acts with impunity. There is no justice.

The question, then, is how does the Establishment commit objectively immoral acts with impunity?

The Establishment power structure—primarily exercised through the claimed authority of its governments—is thousands of years old. It has only become stronger over the centuries and now we face the real prospect of the Establishment harnessing digital technology to shut down all practical avenues of dissent against it and its government system of State authority.

The Establishment rewards those who loyally serve it. It does not admit to punishing those who support it or those who obey its commands—as we’ll discuss in Part 3 it actually punishes most of them on a more-or-less daily basis. Though the occasional tactical sacrifice might be made, the Establishment vigorously safeguards its most effective agents. The Establishment protects its own and itself above all else.

The Establishment has an observable agenda to manipulate and control populations—social engineering. To that end, the Establishment dispatches its agents to regularly commit objectively immoral acts—murder, rape, assault, theft, trespass, deception, and coercion.

The Establishment has developed self-serving systemic control mechanisms—politics, war (of all kinds), usury, propaganda, and censorship, etc. These mechanisms are used by the Establishment, as and when it desires, through government’s claimed legal authority, often exercised by its government’s “legally” approved partners, such as the military-industrial and intelligence complex (public and private), the police, state media, and banks, etc.

The Establishment’s primary command and control system is, therefore, the legal authority claimed by governments. The Establishment then relies upon its government’s legal authority to defend and protect its agents and reinforce its own power. It is through its command and control of this authoritarian system, then, that the Establishment is free to commit objectively immoral acts with impunity. The Establishment doesn’t hold itself to account.

If any of us think that 9/11 was some sort of false flag, or that the official climate change narrative is a deception, or that virology is manipulated science—and therefore no science at all—there are persistent “truths.” All acts and narratives stem from some manner of Establishment deceit, none of them can be realistically challenged through any “legal” or formal processes permitted by the Establishment, and all are the result of immoral acts committed by the Establishment with impunity.

Consequently, we can potentially identify an initial T-Mer truth: The Establishment claims the legal authority to commit objectively immoral acts with impunity.

If prospective T-Mers accept this foundational truth, a real Truth Movement could be formed. Compelling narratives can be presented, campaign objectives can be established, social momentum can be built and a lucid long-term vision of the remedy to the defined problem[s] offered.

Of course, the Establishment denies that it commits objectively immoral acts with impunity. It’s mouthpieces drone on about having to make the tough choices, it occasionally throws one of its own under a bus, and it convenes public inquiries to assuage people’s anger when it gets caught. Many potential T-Mers already know that the tough choices are consistently tough on the people but routinely benefit the Establishment; those sacrificed are usually bit-player stooges, retired on fat pensions, or dead, and public inquiries are government run cover-ups and damage limitation exercises designed to protect the Establishment.

Many people, however, do not appear to appreciate these “truths.” For a myriad of faulty reasons—which we’ll explore—A lot of people either don’t recognise this truth or can’t face up to it. A majority of people think the government is awful but simultaneously believe there’s nothing they can do about it and consequently accept their fate, often choosing to vote for the lesser of two evils.

To build social momentum T-Mers will need to show this latter, sizeable group, that there is something they can do about it. Obviously, in order to do that, T-Mers first have to agree on the truth they are going to pursue. Fortunately, finding T-Mer common ground doesn’t need to be anywhere near as difficult as the Establishment has observably tried to make it.

The fake truth or “truther movement”—previously discussed—has been sold to the public by the Establishment because it mischaracterises people who, through their appreciation of one aspect of the truth or another, have come to question the Establishment to some extent—the Establishment’s so-called truthers.

Simultaneously, the Establishment sells the fake TM to the people it labels as truther’s because, while they think they are part of a movement that does not exist, the potential T-Mers focus only on the facets of anti-Establishment truth that interest them without bothering to form a movement that could pose any threat to the Establishment.

Further, by inserting infiltrators and deceptive information into each of those contained areas of research, the Establishment can easily bog prospective T-Mers down in endless internecine squabbles. Combined, these Establishment strategies ensure that a real TM never forms.

The Establishment goes to these length because it is terrified of those who could unite and become T-Mers in a real Truth Movement. Once we understand why the Establishment is so frightened, the unifying cause that could bond all T-Mers is revealed and thus the compelling narratives, campaign objectives, and long-term-vision of the possible TM start coming into view.

We get an inkling of the reasons for the Establishments’ fear from its mainstream media propagandists. State propaganda divisions, like BBC News, apply a variety of deprecating labels to the people who question Establishment narratives but “conspiracy theorist” is probably the most prevalent. As the BBC is keen to highlight:

Tackling conspiracy theories is “about having trust in our institutions and trust in our journalists to try and pull out the lies.”

It seems the people called conspiracy theorists are undermining “trust in our institutions.” This social phenomenon is, we are led to believe, a problem that needs to be tackled. So who are the conspiracy theorists?

In social psychology, the working—allegedly scientific—definition of “conspiracy theorist” is someone who expresses an opinion that “conflicts with the official story, where the official story is the explanation offered by the (relevant) epistemic authorities.” The “(relevant) epistemic authorities” are “the distributed network of knowledge claim gatherers and testers that includes engineers and politics professors, security experts and journalists”—carefully trained and selected agents of the Establishment in other words.

Succinctly, the official “scientific” definition of a conspiracy theorist—T-Mer candidates—is someone who questions the Establishment or its approved officialnarratives.

The Establishment’s problem that purportedly needs to be tackled, then, is people questioning the Establishment. So serious is the devastating scourge of people doubting the Establishment that it apparently needs to be tackled at the global governance level.

The United Nations (UN) refers to the “epistemic authorities” as the “traditional actors” that serve as the Establishment’s “gatekeepers of information and news.” The UN labels the so-called conspiracy theorists—our prospective T-Mers—as “non-traditional actors in the infosphere” where the infosphere represents the “channels through which information is produced and disseminated.”

Like the majority of the Establishment’s representative bodies, the UN recognises that the internet has greatly increased the number of channels through which information can be shared. This, the UN notes, means “anyone can create and disseminate information.”

According to the UN, this has “democratized the infosphere.” The UN is vehemently opposed to the democratisation of information sharing because questioning the epistemic authorities—as our envisioned T-Mers are liable to do—creates the allegedly problematic “mistrust towards public institutions.”

The Establishment’s evident concerns about the loss of trust in its institutions is well-founded. Even its own statisticians recognise that trust in government is collapsing. Establishment propagandists have invented new terms like “trust deficit” to describe the clear “erosion of trust.” Dismissed and marginalised as they are, the Establishment questioning truthers—or conspiracy theorists—have had a quite remarkable impact on the Establishment it seems. Bluntly, the Establishment is bricking it.

Restoring the supposedly imperative “trust” has become an Establishment obsession. In the private sector, Establishment organisations like the World Economic Forum base entire annual campaign strategies on “rebuilding trust.” In the public sector, governments have formed international alliances whose stated purpose is “to rebuild trust in government and make democracy more meaningful for all.”

All of which is very confusing. The assertion that “trust” in government makes “democracy more meaningful” is historically illiterate dross.

To explain: in 1863 at Gettysburg, Abraham Lincoln noted that an underlying principle of liberty was that “all men are created equal.” This is a rather important point to grasp.

In the subsequent preamble to the UN’s Universal Declaration of Human Rights it is stated that “the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world.” Article 7 of the Declaration adds: “All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law.”

Speaking in 2023 about our endlessly touted equality before the law, then UK Attorney General Victoria Prentis said:

The rule of law is the principle that the law applies equally to everyone, that no one is above the law, and, in particular, that the Government must comply with the law and that power is not exercised arbitrarily.

Establishment agents, like former UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer, laboriously stress that we are all equal before the law and that power isn’t, therefore, arbitrary. Like all other Establishment lackeys, Starmer insists that “no one is above the law.” This is an alleged democratic truth repeatedly impressed upon us.

Returning to Lincoln, he implored the people to honour the ultimate sacrifice made by those who had fought and died at Gettysburg by continuing the lost souls’ struggle for “freedom.” The living could win that struggle and honour the fallen, he suggested, by instituting “government of the people, by the people, for the people.”

We are told this libertarian concept is the foundation of representative democratic governance. The Royal Institute for International Affairs (Chatham House), the Establishment’s most powerful international policy think tank, defines democracy as “government of the people, by the people, for the people.” In the UK, we have just commemorated the military fallen who, it is said, gave their lives to defend our democratic freedoms. Presumably, the civilian fallen were just killed.

If any part of the Establishment’s narrative about the essence of democratic government is true, then the Establishment’s clamour to “rebuild trust” makes no sense whatsoever. In representative democracies, such as the UK’s parliamentary democracy, the people don’t need to “trust” the government or its institutions because the people supposedly rule the government, not vice versa.

Government accountability to the people is said to be a core pillar of the democratic governance. The UK government says “accountability is a fundamental principle” of democracy.

The UK government declares:

“Accountability” means that decision makers are answerable for the decisions they make, the services they deliver and the way they deliver them.

Indeed, “trusting” the government would be extremely unwise given the immense power government claims to wield. The UK government Cabinet Office tells British children, adults with learning difficulties and others who need easy reading:

We are the Cabinet Office. We are part of the government, and we write laws. The government is in charge of running the country. The law is a rule the government says everyone must follow.

Obviously, having the power to decree the rules that “everyone must follow” is a pretty big deal. Especially as this power is enforced through violence, though the government didn’t feel the need to disclose that bit.

Thankfully, we can rest easy because we all reputedly live under a democratic system where every single one of those laws “appl[y] equally to everyone.” Lest we forget, which would be difficult, every official “decision maker,” such as politicians and judges, are “answerable” to everyone else. Just as we all are to each other apparently. It’s the law—a rule the governments says everyone must follow without exception.

Therefore, it is clear that government of, for, and by the people is not based on the idea that anyone needs to trust any “decision makers.” Purported democratic accountability negates the need for the people to trust any decision makers. Just ask the government, the UN, the judiciary, the Establishment’s media, or its historians—the epistemic authorities. They never cease to tell us it is so. None of us need have any doubt.

We don’t have to trust decision makers. This is a is “fundamental principle” of ourdemocracy, is it not?

So why is the Establishment, which fills the airwaves with reminders to us to venerate our relentlessly reported democratic freedoms, haunted by the loss of public trust in its “public institutions,” such as the government?

Another “truth” is that the trust the Establishment is blatantly desperate to restore is crucial for the Establishment to maintain our obedience to it. We should note, obedience isn’t a democratic principle either.

Again, according to the UN:

Trust is central for societies, the State, and markets to function. It is key to building and maintaining social cohesion, as it promotes cooperation between groups of people as well as between people and the State. [. . .] When people perceive institutions as legitimate, fair and efficient, they are more likely to comply with rules [Laws] and uphold their duties and responsibilities. They might be more willing to cooperate, participate and adhere to rules and norms such as paying taxes, complying with government regulations, accepting the rule of law, adhering to contracts, or voting.

To hammer home the point, none of this talk about “trust” has anything to do with any kind of democracy—nominally government of, for, and by the people.

Obviously, we need to trust each other to cooperate in business and in life. We might choose to trust the advice or leadership someone offers. But that trust is not given freely, it is earned or, in the case of employment contracts for example, sold. Trust is maintained by consistently demonstrating trustworthiness. Trust is easily broken and can be readily withdrawn. Trust is contractual if you like.

The “trust” demanded by the Establishments cannot be questioned. If people express any doubt about whatever the Establishment tells them to believe they are marginalised, discredited, censored, and labelled as ne’re-do-wells. Though the Establishment claims the trust it requires is contractual, that contract determines that trust must be given in perpetuity and stipulates that the Establishment has the authority to enforce the trust it demands.

To recap: Questioning the State, and holding decision makers to account, is a fundamental democratic principle. However, the people who exercise their “democratic freedoms,” by questioning the State and trying to hold decision makers to account—i.e., conspiracy theorists, climate deniers, covid refuseniks, whatever—are actively undermining trust in “the State.” By eroding democratically irrelevant trust, they are said to be sabotaging “social cohesion” which is measured by the extent to which people “comply with rules” or “adhere to the norms” ordered by the State.

If, as the UN avers, the Establishment’s strange model of public “trust” is required for the State to function, it can’t possibly be any kind of “democratic state.” Evidently this thing, the State, is divorced from the concept of democracy. It is a separate entity, something other than democratic. So what is the State?

The State can be defined as:

[A] form of human association distinguished from other social groups. Its purpose is to establish order and security using laws, which it enforces within its jurisdiction or geographic boundaries. [. . .] A sovereign state is a political entity with supreme authority within its territorial boundaries. [. . .] Sovereignty means that the state possesses the ultimate authority in decision-making and maintenance of order.

Put another way, the State is a group of people who claim some sort of unique authority—supreme or ultimate authority—to enforce their decisions, or rules. They call the enforcement of their rules “law” or “order.” From where, we might ask, does this social group get its unique, supreme authority?

In 1918, German historian, jurist, and political economist Max Weber said:

[T]he relation between the state and violence is an especially intimate one. [. . .] [A] state is a human community that (successfully) claims the monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force within a given territory. [. . .] The state is considered the sole source of the ‘right’ to use violence.

This successful claim, to be the sole “community” with the right to use violence, is the unique or ultimate authority of the State. The claim is successful because, in more recent modern history, people have been convinced by the Establishment that they live in democratic states and are thus immorally deceived and placated by the Establishment.

For example, State propagandist and former British Home Secretary William Hague alleges that the democratic State exists to “keep in check an over-mighty State.” But we don’t live in democratic states.

Political science clearly demonstrates that we actually live in biased pluralist societies that serve the so-called “economic elite”—functional oligarchies.

The democratic State is a myth.

An oligarch is someone who has used their amassed wealth to buy political influence and sociopolitical authority—State power. Oligarchs form the parasite class, sometimes deferentially referred to as “the elite,” and oligarchs are the leading members of the Establishment.

Therefore, the social group, or human community, that claims the sole right to use violence is the oligarch-led Establishment. The Establishment and the State are synonymous. In turn, the State oversees a biased pluralist governance system. As a jurisdiction, the “country” is a functional oligarchy not a democratic State.

Remember, the UK government says that it runs the country and writes the rules that everyone must follow. Given that the State we live in is actually a functional oligarchy, evidently the government’s claim to run the country and write the rules is a not the “truth.” The government’s claim is also a deceit or a lie.

In “truth,” the Establishment, not the government, runs the biased pluralist State. Some parliamentarians and some other politicians, but not all, are part of the Establishment. Nevertheless, all politicians serve the Establishment’s biased pluralist State as do all governments formed by politicians.

The Establishments can successfully run the State with impunity because sufficient numbers of people believe that, what they wrongly perceive to be their democratic government has a legitimate monopoly on the right to initiate the use of force. This alleged state of affairs is the antipode of everything we are told about democracy.

We are informed that “the equal and inalienable rights of all members of the human family is the foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world;” we are never allowed to forget that “all are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law” and that “no one is above the law;” we are consistently urged to acknowledge that “government must comply with the law and that power is not exercised arbitrarily;” we are educated to think all of this is made possible by “government of the people, by the people, for the people,” and we must embrace, within every fibre of our being, that our corresponding hard won “democratic freedoms” exist to “keep in check an over-mighty State.”

If these core tenets of our supposed system of democratic governance are true then it is impossible for any democratic State to exist in reality. To “enforce” its “supreme authority” on the rest of us, the State claims for itself a slew of purported rights that no one else possesses. There cannot be any equality of rights, and thus no law, no justice, and no peace—ever.

Only the State has the alleged right to initiate the use of force. Only the State claims the right to kill. Only the State can have the so-called right to punish wrongdoers. Only the State supposedly has the right to demand payment with menaces—taxes. Only the State has the apparent right to set the rules and the State claims the further sole right to declare those rules “laws” that “everyone [else] must follow.” Only the State can commit these objectively immoral acts with impunity.

The State is nothing other than a “social group” that says it is a “political entity” with the seized “ultimate authority in decision-making.” This group—the State—maintains the “order” that it “decrees.” The ruling social group is not equal with the rest of us. We are, by the State’s purported rule of law, subservient to them. As we have just discussed, that social group is the oligarch-led Establishment.

To maintain a belief in the so-called “democratic State” you have to concede that not all “members of the human family” have “equal [. . .] rights.” As Lincoln stressed, all “men are created equal.” This is a cardinal doctrine of democracy—supposedly. Rationally, you can’t both acknowledge that one social group possesses rights that no others have and simultaneously maintain that the society we call a representative democracy is a democracy.

The Establishment obviously gives itself additional rights and rejects the “foundation of freedom, justice and peace in the world” outright.

Moreover, the Establishment devolves its immoral authority to the faux “democratic State” represented by its agent, the government. The whole claim of authority is founded on the unmistakable fact that we are not all “equal before the law.” If we were then we would all have the equal immoral right to initiate the use of force and all government authority would instantly vanish.

Yet, this still doesn’t fully explain why, with all that illegitimate State power in its hands, the Establishment is so frightened of losing everyone’s “trust?” The “truth” explains it.

The truth is that the Establishment’s contention that it is the only group that can legitimately initiate the use of force is entirely reliant on people’s trust in its “public institutions.” The word “trust,” in this context, means: Firm belief in the reliability, truth, or ability of someone or something.

The overwhelming majority of the populations still holds the “firm belief” that the government’s insistence that its authority is legitimate is reliably the “truth.” But that trust is based solely on the stories they are told about a democratic State that cannot and does not function as those stories depict. The people labelled as conspiracy theorists—the marginalised truthers—have used the new “channels through which information is produced and disseminated” to question and challenge those stories.

It is evident that the Establishment is making an enormous effort to reassure the wider public that nothing our envisaged T-Mers say is true. Nonetheless, despite the Establishment’s staunch defence, the information T-Mers are propagating is seeping into the general public’s consciousness. If it wasn’t, the Establishment wouldn’t bother with the global propaganda campaigns, censorship strategies, and lawfare it is using to try to plug the leak.

While the population predominantly remains wedded to the idea that the State is democratic, and while most people continue to believe that the government is in charge, they aren’t likely to be overly concerned about the Establishment. Though many people, perhaps the majority, have a general awareness of what the Establishment is, they don’t fully acknowledge, or feel safe to ignore, the Establishment.

This is because of their misplaced “trust” in the democratic State. It blinds them to the “truth” about the Establishment: the Establishment is “the whole matrix of official and social relations within which [all] power is exercised.”

Should the public’s “trust” in the Establishment’s “public institutions”—especially government—be shaken further, the Establishment will face major problems. If the people come to appreciate what the Establishment actually is and how it operates, the oligarch-led Establishment is in deep trouble.

Establishment authority is nothing more than the populations trust in the veracity of the State’s claim to posses that authority. If the general public becomes actively conscious of the fact that the State’s so-called authority is merely its assertion that only it has the right to be violent, then, the public’s “trust” will rapidly disappear.

In the absence of that trust, all the Establishment has left is brute force and it lacks the numbers to successfully rule for long purely through violence—initiation of the use of force. Ultimately, sustaining the people’s conformity is the Establishment’s only survival strategy. Once public obedience, or “trust” as the Establishment likes to call it, is gone, the Establishment is finished.

Blatantly, for the oligarch-led Establishment, the loss of public “trust” is its Achilles’ heel. For any future TM, shattering “trust” in the Establishment’s fabricated “authority” is a clear strategic goal.

The Establishment’s evident panic tells us a lot. Its claimed authority is a feeble charade that, once perceived, crumbles. The Establishment is not powerful and it is running scared. It’s State is not “mighty” at all. It is weak and vulnerable. If ever there was an opportune moment for a real Truth Movement it is now.

If all T-Mers can agree that, regardless of whatever aspect of the truth they are particularly interested in, the overarching problem is the Establishment’s misuse of illegitimate authority, then forming a real Truth Movement is eminently achievable.

I am forwarding my anarchist perspective of illegitimate authority but our would-be T-Mers don’t need to be anarchists to appreciate the truth about the Establishment or its fictitious authority. Nor do the solutions need to be anarchist, though some appreciation of genuine anarchist philosophy would help. There is, I contend, a reason why, of all sociopolitical theories, the Establishment denigrates anarchism more than any other.

The Establishment—immorally deceiving the people into believing that its fabricated anti-democratic system embodies government of, by, and for the people—has socially engineered the widespread misconception that there is no alternative to its oppressive, violent system. In Part 3, we’ll discuss the extensive range of solutions to Establishment rule that, contrary to Establishment claims, are perfectly feasible.

So we can expand the possible Truth Movement’s foundational truth:

  • The Establishment claims that only it has the right to initiate the use of force—violence. The Establishment calls its exclusive use of violence its “authority.” This immoral claim of authority is contrary to all democratic principles. The Truth Movement rejects all forms of violence. Therefore, the Truth Movement rejects the Establishment’s alleged authority. The Truth Movement demands an end to Establishment rule. The Truth Movement stands for genuine freedom, justice and peace in the world.

A lofty ambition perhaps, but is it unreasonable? As prospective T-Mers, do we think people don’t want to live in freedom, justice, and peace?

How do we, the prospective T-Mers who have been ostracised by the Establishment and everyone who still believes in the Establishment’s authority; we, who dare to question the Establishment’s narratives and, by exercising our supposed democratic freedoms, have become the number one enemy of the Establishment and its State, reach out to the disillusioned millions who see no alternative. Because they are the people with whom the Truth Movement could most certainly build social momentum.

How do we unite when we have been so bitterly divided, largely thanks, but not solely due, to the efforts of the Establishment? What long-term vision can we offer to solve the problem of the Establishment’s immoral dictatorship?

That is what we’ll discuss in the concluding Part 3.

articles.title: Attacks on Christians in Europe Surge 44%, Nearly 2,500 Anti-Christian Incidents Reported
articles.content:
by Emmitt Barry, Worthy News Washington D.C. Bureau Chief

(Worthy News) – Attacks targeting Christians across Europe surged 44% in 2025, according to a new report documenting nearly 2,500 anti-Christian hate crimes and incidents, raising fresh concerns about religious persecution and growing restrictions on Christian expression across the continent.

The Vienna-based Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians in Europe (OIDAC Europe) reported 2,465 incidents in its annual report released November 16, including 395 attacks against individuals involving physical violence, threats, and harassment, compared with 274 the previous year.

France recorded the highest number of government-documented incidents at 843, followed by England and Wales with 624, Germany with 337, and Austria with 134. In France, offenses against individual Christians increased 70%, while physical assaults against clergy quadrupled.

Most incidents involved attacks on churches, cemeteries, and Christian property, including vandalism, desecration, and arson.

Among the most disturbing cases was the September 2025 murder of Ashur Sarnaya, an Assyrian Christian refugee from Iraq who was stabbed to death in Lyon, France, while livestreaming Christian messages. The report also documented the murder of a Catholic priest in Poland.

Growing Restrictions on Christian Religious Freedom

Beyond physical attacks, the report warned of mounting legal and institutional pressures against Christians, including employment discrimination, restrictions on public prayer, and prosecutions involving peaceful religious expression.

Cases highlighted included Christian teachers losing employment after expressing biblical convictions about abortion and individuals facing criminal proceedings for praying or conducting religious services near abortion facilities.

OIDAC Europe called on the European Union to appoint a dedicated coordinator to combat anti-Christian hatred, similar to existing positions addressing antisemitism and anti-Muslim discrimination.

The organization also warned that inconsistent reporting and underreporting could conceal the full extent of anti-Christian hostility, while differences in national recording methods complicate comparisons.

The findings underscore growing concerns that Christians in Europe face not only violence against their places of worship but increasing challenges to openly practicing and expressing their faith.

The post Attacks on Christians in Europe Surge 44%, Nearly 2,500 Anti-Christian Incidents Reported appeared first on Worthy Christian News.

articles.title: No company or university anywhere in the world has ever apologized for their COVID vaccine mandates
articles.content:
Executive summary

I did an AI search recently to find out if any company or university has publicly apologized for their COVID mandate policy.

Is an apology warranted?

The peer-reviewed literature says YES.

The Bardosh paper “COVID-19 vaccine boosters for young adults: a risk benefit assessment and ethical analysis of mandate policies at universities” argued that college vaccine mandates were unethical because the near-zeo benefits didn’t strongly outweigh the harms. But then the same journal that published the Bardosh paper (BMJ Journal of Medical Ethics) published a counter-argument by Lam and Nichols, “Ethics of college vaccine mandates, using reasonable comparisons.” The Bardosh authors subsequently published a rebuttal to the Lam paper, “University-age vaccine mandates: reply to Lam and Nichols.”

Most people would be hopelessly confused at this point.

Who is actually right?

This is where it helps to have a tool like AlterAI to help you sort through all the arguments. Here’s the full conversation.

The answer, if you are objectively judging the arguments, is that the Bardosh authors were correct. The vaccines were clearly unethical for university students because the claimed benefits were vastly outweighed by the risks. For example, the vaccine RCTs never showed a mortality benefit associated with the vaccine; if it existed, it was literally too small to measure. Yet the COVID vaccine killed people… over 1 per 1,000 by my estimates (over 250,000 Americans killed by the COVID shots).

Yet, not a single company or university anywhere in the world has apologized for their error.

And the error in mandating the shots should have been crystal clear during Omicron where it was very clear that the vaccines provided no benefit, yet the mandates persisted; no apologies even after it was painfully obvious.

Summary

Even when the data is crystal clear, companies and universities seem to have a hard time admitting they demanded a COVID mandate that was unjustified and resulted in permanent disability or death of hundreds of thousands of Americans.

Do you think we’ll ever hear from an honest company or university admitting they were wrong? Or will they just silently drop the mandates and hope we all forget the harm they caused?

Share

articles.title: In Honor of Ray Yungen (1952-2016) – The Man Who Inspired the Birth of Lighthouse Trails
articles.content:
Ten years ago, in October of 2016, Ray Yungen passed away after contracting sepsis during a hospital stay for treatment of leukemia. There’s not a day that goes by at the office of Lighthouse Trails where Ray’s name does not come in at least one conversation. We still miss him so much. Without him, we don’t believe there ever would have been a Lighthouse Trails. In honor of Ray, during this ten-year mark, we are re-posting below our booklet, The Story Behind Lighthouse Trails.

The Story Behind Lighthouse Trails

By Deborah Dombrowski and the Editors at Lighthouse Trails

“It Was a Dark and Stormy Night.”

Every good mystery starts off with “It was a dark and stormy night.” But this is a different kind of mystery. It’s about a church, a Bride, that was mysteriously kidnapped by a dark, deceitful stranger who came as an angel of light and promised her many great things if she would just follow him. And it’s about a small insignificant publishing company who teamed up with members of the Bride who did not succumb to the angel of light, in an effort to find out what happened the Bride and how to bring her back to safety.

In the summer of 2000, there was no Lighthouse Trails Publishing. There wasn’t even a glimmer in anyone’s mind about it. Dave and I were nearing the final round of raising a half a dozen kids in a small town in Oregon, one nestled in the Cascade foothills. We had been alerted in 1997 to a thing called Y2K and helped put together a task force in our little town. Not because we thought the world was coming to an end on December 31, 1999. We didn’t. But we were stirred from our every day lives of soccer games, raising kids, going to church, small time campaigning to keep the homosexual agenda out of the schools, helping friends in need, supporting ministries like Focus on the Family—you know, just the regular stuff a good Christian family does. In twenty-five years of being part of the church after getting saved in the ’70s (I in a barn with a Bible and some cows, Dave in army barracks in Germany), there were a lot of things we had never heard about in the pulpits. At first, in the ’70s, we heard a lot about Jesus’ return, and it wasn’t unusual to hear the Gospel preached on Sundays with people going forward in altar calls and getting saved. It was exciting, and there was anticipation in the air that the rapture could happen at any time. But over time, that kind of talk ceased, altar calls died down and were replaced with lots of other things: signs and wonders that were said to all be from God, boycotts and legislation efforts to turn our country into a “Christian” culture, songs that started leaving Jesus and the Cross out, and in many cases drums so loud, you wouldn’t be able to hear the words anyway, or songs about all the great things we could do if we would just unite together.

When Y2K came, it jolted us and reminded us that our time on this earth is very temporal, and the Bible talks about a time where people will become very deceived, not realizing the times in which we live. While we did not believe that the culmination of time would end at the strike of midnight on New Year’s Eve 1999, we did believe God wanted to get our attention. We just weren’t sure what for at the time. 2000 rolled in rather uneventfully, and life continued. However, in 1998 an elderly acquaintance we met during Y2K had told us about an author she knew in Salem (Oregon) who wrote about how the New Age was coming into the evangelical church. While we knew something about the New Age, it was a term that was never mentioned in the pulpit of any church we had ever been to, so the remark slipped quietly away for two years.

In the fall of 2000, our then sixteen-year-old daughter was a Young Life intern. Young Life is a national organization that reaches out to young people in public schools with a Christian message. One day in October, she brought home a list of required reading for the year. It contained books by twelve authors, most of whom we nor our daughter had ever heard of. Four of them would soon change our lives forever: Thomas Merton, Richard Foster, Henri Nouwen, and Brennan Manning.

About a week later, a local pastor called because he was trying to get some information about a college his kids wanted to go to. “Deborah, remember you told me a couple years ago about an author around here who wrote about the New Age coming into the church? I wonder if you can find out about that.” After that call, I contacted my friend who had told me about this author, and she immediately said, “Deborah, it’s time you met Ray Yungen.”

A week later, I sat in a Keizer, Oregon coffee shop, a few minutes early for my appointment with Mr. Yungen. Right on time, in bounded a 6’4” pleasant looking kind of guy carrying in each arm bundles of magazines, newspaper clippings, and books. After plopping down his obviously well-read stacks of materials, he bought me a fifty-cent cup of house coffee then proceeded to talk to me for over an hour. When early in the talk, he mentioned Thomas Merton and Richard Foster, something told me this was a providential meeting. And when a little later he mentioned Brennan Manning and Henri Nouwen, I was beginning to get the picture. This man had been sent to save my daughter from reading books by men who called themselves Christians but who, in reality, were bringing a mystical spirituality under the guise of Christianity. Before I left that meeting with Ray, he handed me a brown envelope. “I’ve written a book about this, but it isn’t published yet. I call it A Time of Departing. I’ve been carrying it around for two years. I wonder if you and your husband would like to read it.” I took the package and left.

It would be an understatement to say that reading that manuscript opened our eyes and changed our lives forever. And if someone had told us back then that in less than two years from that day in the coffee shop we would start a publishing company and eventually take on the Christian leaders in North America, we probably would have run the other way. Frankly, at the time, we thought Ray Yungen’s book came just in time to help warn the church so contemplative spirituality would not enter it. We thought that there could be no way that too many Christians would even consider going down the contemplative path. It just seemed so obvious to us how dangerous and anti-biblical it was. We thought that if we could warn some of the more influential leaders (like Rick Warren), they would be so happy to be warned, they would probably go out and write their own books warning about contemplative prayer, and we could just go back to our “normal” lives and leave this kind of thing up to them.

We had a lot of misconceived thoughts in those days, and we had no idea what was about to happen.

Part 2
A Ministry Is Born

After reading the unpublished manuscript, A Time of Departing by Ray Yungen (our newfound brother in the faith) in the fall of 2000, the first thing that seemed reasonable to do was to meet with the Young Life Director of Training for Oregon. I was concerned about my own daughter’s involvement with Young Life but also was thinking about all the thousands of Young Life leaders and interns who might be introduced to contemplative spirituality through Young Life’s recommended reading list.

I called the Young Life office in Portland and made an appointment. During the week or so interim before the meeting, I began researching contemplative spirituality on the Internet. The only problem was, there was virtually nothing opposing it or critiquing it. But there was plenty supporting it. Finally, I found an article by a John Caddock (from Oregon). His article was written in 1997 and was titled “What is Contemplative Spirituality, and Why is it So Dangerous?” It was actually a review of Brennan Manning’s book, The Signature of Jesus. That was one of the books Ray had discussed in his manuscript. John Caddock’s article and one other one were the only things on the Internet refuting this mystical prayer that was being called Christian. Essentially, the contemplative issue was not being challenged. Little did we know at the time, it had been simmering in the background within the evangelical church for at least two decades by then and was about to explode wide open.

The day before Ray and I were to meet with the Young Life Director, I stumbled upon Peter Marshall Jr.’s name on the Internet and saw where he was promoting Henri Nouwen. I didn’t know a lot about Marshall Jr., but I had loved the movie of his father Peter Marshall, A Man Called Peter, a Scottish minister who eventually became U.S. Senate Chaplain back in the ’50s.  When I saw the endorsement of Nouwen by Peter Marshall Jr., I e-mailed his office with my concerns and got a rather scathing reply back. In my naivety at the time, I couldn’t believe the e-mail was really from Mr. Marshall. So on the morning I was to leave for my appointment with Ray and the Young Life Director, I called the Peter Marshall office. Lo and behold, Peter Marshall, Jr. answered the phone. He acknowledged that it was indeed he who had written the e-mail, and he told me that anyone who would say anything bad about Henri Nouwen or Brennan Manning was committing “Satanic slander.” Marshall expressed strong anger about my having questioned the two contemplative men. I was very taken back by the angry response to what I had thought was an amiable and mild challenge on my part. When Marshall was finished reprimanding me, we said good-bye and hung up. I never had another chance to talk to Peter Marshall Jr., and he died in 2010 at the age of seventy.

When I arrived at the coffee shop in Portland later that morning, Ray was standing in the foyer waiting for me. As I approached him, I said, “You’ll never believe who I just talked to.” I will never forget Ray’s reaction as I shared what had happened. His eyes filled with tears, and he said, “Peter Marshall is a conservative Christian. I am shocked that he would have such a view.” I knew then that Ray Yungen was a brother who did not hate these people but rather had a genuine desire to help people. And as for Marshall’s angry reaction, I later came to find out that an angry reaction was a common denominator from those who promote contemplative spirituality when challenged by someone about it. While not all of the following names had angry responses, the list of those I would someday talk to either by phone, e-mail, or letter began with Marshall but would later include: Philip Yancey, Dan Kimball, Shane Claiborne, Rick Warren, Ken Blanchard, David Jeremiah, Gary Thomas, Keri Wyatt Kent, Richard Foster (indirectly), Kay Arthur’s personal assistant, personnel from Focus on the Family, Beth Moore’s top assistant as well as Charles Stanley’s close assistant, and many others.

From the fall of 2000, when we met Ray, until the end of 2001, we tried to find a publisher who would publish A Time of Departing. We put together a proposal and sent it out to several Christian publishers.

As one rejection letter after the next came in, we grew more and more skeptical that we would find a publisher for A Time of Departing. In the meantime, Ray read in an article somewhere that the top forty Christian publishers would only publish books written by authors who had “significant national platforms.” We knew this left Ray out. He was unknown.

As for Ray’s writing background, he had written For Many Shall Come in My Name (1st edition) in the early nineties, which was published by a small publishing company that eventually went out of business. The book was an exposé on the New Age movement in our society. Several thousand copies of the book had sold, and Ray did a national tour that included interviews with places like Southwest Radio Church, but when Ray’s publisher went under, he was left without any representation.

Then, in 1994, a few years after Ray wrote For Many Shall Come in My Name, he was asked by a Salem (Oregon) Missionary Alliance youth pastor to research a man named Richard Foster who would be coming to the pastor’s church soon. Ray had not heard about Foster prior to that time, so before the seminar took place, he read Celebration of Discipline. Ray had been studying the Catholic monk and panentheist Thomas Merton for some time, and as he read Foster, he felt there was a connection between him and Merton. Ray attended the seminar and afterwards went to the front where Foster was standing and talking to people. Ray describes the brief conversation he had with Foster that evening:

After the seminar ended . . . I approached Foster and politely asked him, “What do you think of the current Catholic contemplative prayer movement?” He appeared visibly uncomfortable with the question, and at first seemed evasive and vague.

He then replied, “Well, I don’t know, some good, some bad (mentioning Matthew Fox as an example of the bad).” In defense, he said, “My critics don’t understand there is this tradition within Christianity that goes back centuries.” He then said something that has echoed in my mind ever since that day. He emphatically stated, “Well, Thomas Merton tried to awaken God’s people!” I realized then Foster had waded deep into Merton’s belief system.1

Ray began to study Richard Foster in depth after that, and in early 1999, he finished the manuscript of A Time of Departing, with Richard Foster and Thomas Merton as key figures in his critique.  Nearly two years later, we met Ray.

While we were seeking a publisher for A Time of Departing and getting a growing stack of rejection letters, Ron, the Salem youth pastor who had invited Ray to the Richard Foster seminar, was at a church conference and found himself sharing a dining table with John Armstrong, a pastor, author, and an adjunct professor at Wheaton College Graduate School. Ron happened to have a copy of Ray’s manuscript with him, and after striking up a conversation, asked Armstrong if he would take the manuscript with him and read it. Armstrong agreed.

Within a couple weeks, Armstrong contacted Ron and said that A Time of Departing was fantastic. He said if Ray would remove chapter six (“Could This Really Be the End of the Age?”), he could probably get Harvest House to publish the book. At first, we were excited, but after prayer and deliberation, Ray, Dave, and I decided that removing that chapter would seriously diminish the message of the book. It is in that chapter that Ray talks about occultist Alice Bailey (who coined the term New Age) and her prediction that the Age of Aquarius (a supposed age of enlightenment for man when he realizes his divinity) would come through the Christian church by mystical practices and signs and wonders. Chapter six also talks about what the Bible refers to as Mystery Babylon (Revelation 17:5) where seducing spirits will deceive the whole world into embracing a new system of spirituality (a one-world religion). Quoting from that chapter, Ray stated:

[I]nstead of opposing Christianity, the occult would capture and blend itself with Christianity and then use it as its primary  vehicle for spreading and instilling New Age consciousness!2

No, we knew that chapter had to stay. Sadly, and ironically, John Armstrong eventually came out as an advocate for the emerging church.

One day, after we turned down John Armstrong’s offer to help publish A Time of Departing and after we were beginning to think we would never find a publisher for this vitally important book, a little light came on, so to speak, and I said to Dave, “Why don’t we start our own publishing company and publish the book ourselves?”  We prayed that God would open the door if that’s what He wanted us to do, and after talking to Ray, we mutually agreed that this was how we could get the book published.

We knew nothing about publishing. I was a small-time free-lance writer and had written, Laughter Calls Me, my own biography, and Dave had a degree in English from Portland State University. But that hardly prepared us to start a publishing company. I bought a bunch of books from Amazon, one of which was called How to Publish a Book and Sell a Million Copies. It seemed only logical that if we were going to publish a book, selling a million copies would certainly get our message out. However, when I read that book, one of the things it advised was, don’t publish anything “controversial” if you are interested in “large sales.” It was then I knew that Lighthouse Trails would never be a big publishing company that sold millions of books. We started off controversial, and nearly twenty-five years later, we are still considered controversial. Sadly, “controversial” is increasingly coming to mean “something devoted to the biblical Gospel.”

In March of 2002, we opened a business bank account with one hundred dollars and officially started Lighthouse Trails Publishing. Our motto would be “bringing light to areas of darkness.” Six months later, we released the first edition of A Time of Departing.

Part 3

“A Hot Topic” That Just Wouldn’t Go Away”

Right about the same time as A Time of Departing was being released, another book, by a large Christian publishing house, was also being released. While we were picking up the first printing of our new release from a small printer in Washington state, unbeknownst to us at the time, Rick Warren’s The Purpose Driven Life was being released as well and would soon be a New York Times best seller, eventually reaching sales of over 35 million copies. It would turn into a rabbit versus a turtle race to get our messages out, but because we believed that contemplative spirituality would draw people away from the Gospel rather than to it, we felt our efforts were necessary and that God would get our warning out as He saw fit.

In the spring of 2003, we sent a copy of A Time of Departing to Rick Warren thinking we should warn this now-popular pastor of the contemplative prayer movement. He wrote back a personal note on a card saying:

Just a note to say thanks for the copy of A Time of Departing by Ray Yungen. It definitely will be a useful addition to my personal library and resource in my studies. I agree this is a hot topic.

Sincerely, Rick Warren

When we received Rick Warren’s reply, we felt a sense of relief that he seemed to have appreciated our warning. But that was before a lot of things happened:

  • It was before we read
    • Deceived on Purpose: The New Age Implications of the Purpose Driven Life by former New Age follower Warren B. Smith.
    • It was before we learned that Rick Warren had been promoting Richard Foster, Dallas Willard, and the spiritual formation (i.e., contemplative spirituality) movement as far back as the early nineties in his first book, The Purpose Driven Church.3
    • It was before we read George Mair’s book, A Life With Purpose: Reverend Rick Warren—the most inspiring pastor of our time which identified Rick Warren’s plans to use New Age sympathizer Ken Blanchard for his global P.E.A.C.E. Plan in training leaders around the world.4
    • It was before George Mair was advised by an acquaintance at the Attorney General’s office in California to file a hate crime against Rick Warren for his assault against Mair for his book (but Mair called me, and I advised him against filing).5 Ironically, when Mair wrote his book, it was meant to be a testament of praise to Rick Warren as “America’s Pastor” not realizing that at the same time New Age connections had been unveiled.
    • It was before Rick Warren wrote his damage-control “midnight e-mail” to me in the spring of 2005, an e-mail that was filled with inaccuracies to cover up the truth, but yet he had his chief apologist at the time post it all over the Internet within hours of sending it to me.6
    • It was before Saddleback sent out e-mails to an undisclosed number of people saying that Lighthouse Trails and Ray Yungen were “sitting on a pile of money” (and we just wanted to know where it was because we could really have used that pile of money to pay the bills that month).
    • It was before Saddleback accused Lighthouse Trails of “publishing lies” and inferring that we had broken into their website server and “federal agents” were on the case.7
    • It was back when we thought there was no way the majority of Christian leaders could be right in the middle of helping to bring in a mystical spirituality that would take millions into the arms of outright apostasy.

    Needless to say, by the time we went to press with the second edition of A Time of Departing in the spring of 2006, the book now had an entire chapter devoted to Rick Warren and his contemplative prayer propensities. And it had a chapter devoted to something everyone was calling “the emerging church.” Vicious and unscrupulous efforts were already underway to stop Lighthouse Trails. Had it been just our own strength and wisdom to keep us going, we never could have continued. But, in spite of our own human frailties and weaknesses, and in spite of efforts to stop us, God showed mercy and justice and kept Lighthouse Trails afloat. And while there’s no question that contemplative spirituality has skyrocketed exponentially throughout the world, thanks largely to big name advocates of the movement, tens of thousands of people have now read A Time of Departing as well as our 2007 book on the emerging church, Faith Undone by Roger Oakland; and we believe these books have made a difference in helping to defend the Gospel message of Jesus Christ and identifying the mystical spirituality that is working to blind the eyes of millions.

    There’s much more to our story, and you can read about most of the episodes on our site. When we first began, we wondered if there were other Christians who saw what Ray, Dave, and I saw. Surely, we can’t be the only ones, we thought. We are so happy to report that we aren’t by a long shot. Through the thousands of e-mails, letters, and phone calls from readers, customers, and newsletter subscribers, we have learned that God has faithfully shown many believers what is happening in today’s church and world. We are privileged and humbled to have a small part in this work. As we have said many times before, Lighthouse Trails exists as a service to the body of Christ, for the sake of the Gospel, and we pray and hope, to the glory of God.

    But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness. Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober. (1Thessalonians 5:1-6)

    Endnotes:
    1. Ray Yungen, A Time of Departing (Eureka, MT: Lighthouse Trails Publishing, 2nd ed., 2006), pp. 76-77.
    2. Ibid., p. 123.
    3. Rick Warren, The Purpose Driven Church (Grand Rapids, MI: Zondervan, 1995), pp. 126-127.
    4. http://www.lighthousetrailsresearch.com/PressReleasekenblanchard.htm.
    5. Read our article “Rick Warren Biographer, George Mair, Passes Away at 83 – The Rest of the Story” for this full story.
    6. http://www.lighthousetrailsresearch.com/furtherinformation.htm.
    7. In December of 2005 a woman sent us an e-mail she had received from Rick Warren’s personal e-mail address, which stated:

    The website you refer to [Lighthouse Trails] below is well-known for publishing lies, which can easily be proven false…. The Bible says “Satan is the father of lies”, so those who intentionally spread them are doing Satan’s work for him. That is evil. We suggest you avoid listening to evil people who have a habit of lying about ministers of the Gospel. Study the Scriptures every day and flee from those who make their reputation by lying.

    We contacted Saddleback about the e-mail, and we received the following reply, suggesting that the e-mail had been written by a computer hacker: “We are sorry that this public mailbox has been written by a computer hacker: “We are sorry that this public mailbox has been shut down due to vandalism and stolen identity. Federal enforcement officers are tracking down the source in either Africa or the Pacific Northwest.” At first, we thought this was a joke because we (who live in the Pacific Northwest) had recently issued a press release about an evangelist in Africa who had been opposing Purpose Driven. Hearing that Federal officers had narrowed down an investigation to either our location or the evangelist’s location seemed preposterous. We contacted Saddleback by phone requesting the names of these Federal agents because of the threatening nature of the “anonymous” email. A few days later a Saddleback staff member called and told us that Federal agents were doing an investigation on their web server being broken into and that Saddleback (and the agents) suspected Lighthouse Trails. We again asked for the names of the Federal agents as well as the Saddleback communications director that was handling the case. However, we were told they would not give us any names. We have not heard anything from Saddleback since.

articles.title: Measles Vaccine Is A Gain-of-Function Lab Product; Infects More Cells Than Wild Virus
articles.content:
This post was published by Jon Fleetwood. Support him by subscribing at Substack and following at Instagram / X / Facebook.

On the mainstream virological model, a May 2016 publication in The Journal of Infectious Diseases by U.S. military biodefense experts states that the live-attenuated measles vaccine was created by a process that “could be considered, by current definitions, GOF research.”

The paper states: “The live-attenuated measles vaccine was created by passaging the virus until mutations arose that altered virus tropism—a technique that could be considered, by current definitions, GOF research.”

On the same model, tropism refers to which cells and tissues a virus can productively infect. According to the literature, the measles vaccine strain (primarily Edmonston lineage) acquired the ability to use CD46 as a receptor during laboratory experiments. Wild-type measles virus is described as primarily using CD150 (SLAM), a receptor largely restricted to activated immune cells, while CD46 is expressed on most human nucleated cells.

Meaning: the virus in the measles vaccine can infect more human cells than the wild measles virus can.

A 2009 review by Diane E. Griffin and Chien-Hsiung Pan (“Measles: Old Vaccines, New Vaccines”) states that “CD46 is principally a receptor for vaccine strains, such as Edmonston, whereas SLAM… permits entry of wild-type MV.” The same paper states that “wild-type isolates typically use SLAM… whereas attenuated vaccine strains… preferentially use CD46.”

According to the mainstream virological-genetic literature, specific amino-acid changes in the hemagglutinin protein (including N481Y and E451V) enable this CD46 binding. These changes are described as having arisen during serial tissue-culture passaging (lab experiments) and are not characteristic of circulating wild-type strains. See, for example, studies such as Nielsen et al., “Adaptation of wild-type measles virus to CD46 receptor usage” (2001).

A 2022 Congressional Research Service report defines gain-of-function as “any genetic mutation in an organism that confers a new or enhanced ability” and notes that scientists can induce such changes experimentally. The American Society for Microbiology describes gain-of-function techniques as those used to “alter the function of an organism in such a way that it is able to do more than it used to do.”

The measles vaccine virus is the product of gain-of-function.

Congress, the White House, the Department of Energy, the FBI, the CIA, and Germany’s Federal Intelligence Service (BND) all acknowledge that the deadly COVID-19 pandemic and subsequent authoritarian response were “likely” the result of gain-of-function laboratory experiments.

Ninety-five percent (95%) of infants develop fever after measles vaccination, and 16% develop more serious measles-like symptoms, according to a December 2025 BMC Infectious Diseases publication.

The most popular measles vaccine (MMRII) is intentionally not tested for carcinogenesis (causing cancer), mutagenesis (causing genetic mutations), or impairment of fertility.

No peer-reviewed studies directly compare the infectivity or replication of the measles vaccine virus versus wild-type virus in living humans. Such head-to-head human challenge studies have not been performed.

Meaning: health officials have no direct comparative human data on which to base claims that the vaccine strain is less infectious or replicates less than wild-type virus inside living people.

Even on mainstream-accepted disease models.

articles.title: Feds Sold Bioweapons-Capable Lab Equipment For $29
articles.content:
This post was published by Jon Fleetwood. Support him by subscribing at Substack and following at Instagram / X / Facebook.

The Government Accountability Office’s September 1, 2026 report (GAO-26-107729, full PDF here) documents that the Department of Health and Human Services and the U.S. Department of Agriculture sold 1,316 pieces of “unneeded” laboratory equipment through the General Services Administration in fiscal years 2022–2025.

Nine of those items (three freeze dryers and six mass spectrometers) sat on the Commerce Control List because “they could be used by certain countries of concern to develop biological weapons or to gain a military advantage.”

The agencies never told GSA (General Services Administration) the items were controlled, as federal rules required.

One buyer took two of the controlled pieces plus more than 100 other HHS items, including DNA analyzers and sequencers.

Officials could not establish how any of it was used.

Two freeze dryers originally bought for roughly $12,000 and $25,000 sold for $29 and $208.

  • Who decided these sales were acceptable?
  • Why did no one at HHS or USDA assess the risk that the same equipment could help someone produce biological weapons or extract sensitive genetic data?
  • Why did a single buyer accumulate over 100 pieces while agencies had no answer on the ultimate destination?

The report was requested by House Energy and Commerce leaders including Chairman Brett Guthrie, Gary Palmer, H. Morgan Griffith, John Joyce, and Earl “Buddy” Carter after a February 2024 request.

The committee later described the findings as exposing the U.S. to a “severe bioterrorism threat.”

articles.title: Feds Drop $117M On Under-Skin ‘SENTINEL’ Sensors To Track Your Body 24/7
articles.content:
This post was published by Jon Fleetwood. Support him by subscribing at Substack and following at Instagram / X / Facebook.

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) announced October 1, 2026, that its Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) is committing up to $117.4 million to develop technology for continuously monitoring activity inside human bodies, including medication levels, hormones, and immune markers, with federally funded devices capable of penetrating the skin and transmitting biological readings wirelessly.

The program, called Delphi, explicitly targets:

“continuous, real-time monitoring of deep biological signals for everyone.”

The feds are financing technology that could turn Americans’ bodies into continuously monitored sources of digital information.

The federal program description also confirms plans for widespread commercial adoption.

  • Who will control the information?

  • Could insurers, employers, or government agencies use biological readings to enforce medication compliance?

  • Could authorities classify individuals as public-health threats using measurements taken directly from their bodies?

  • Could refusing to share those measurements eventually carry consequences?

The unavoidable implication is that whoever controls access to these readings could gain the ability to monitor Americans’ medication use and biological activity without relying on what individuals voluntarily disclose.

The government is financing that capability while leaving fundamental questions about informed consent, data access, and future institutional use unanswered in its public program disclosures.

Feds Want Biological Tracking ”for Everyone”

ARPA-H identifies the intended measurements as: “hormones, immune markers, and therapeutic drug levels.”

That last category is particularly consequential.

Measuring drug levels could allow someone with access to the readings to check whether an individual has taken medication.

The agency also intends to: “build open, reusable architectures and standards that industry alone cannot develop.”

And to: “Lower the barriers for bold prototypes that can be scaled and adopted by healthcare and consumer markets.”

In plain English, the feds want different companies to build compatible biological monitoring devices using shared technological standards.

articles.title: The Continuation of the Roman Empire
articles.content:
866-295-4143,

fbns@wayoflife.org

The Roman Empire existed in the east as the Byzantine Empire headquartered in Constantinople, which continued until the city was conquered by the Muslims in 1453.

The Roman Empire continued in the Holy Roman Empire, which began with the coronation of Charlemagne by Pope Leo III in AD 800. Charlemagne wanted to establish a Christian Roman Empire. Called “the father of Europe,” he united most of central Europe and laid the foundation for a Catholic Europe that featured a unity of church and state.

Napoleon (1769-1821) aspired to restore the Roman Empire. He established an imperial system based on Rome’s. When he was coronated by Pope Pius VII in Paris in 1804, he was crowned with two crowns: one made of a golden laurel wreath, recalling ancient Rome, and one being a replica of Charlemagne’s (Andrew Roberts,

Napoleon: A Life, p. 355). By 1812, the French Empire in Europe covered much of the territory controlled by ancient Rome. That year, Napoleon said, “I am a true Roman Emperor; I am of the best race of the Caesars--those who are founders.” Napoleon’s troops marched with a standard bearing the Roman eagle. He commissioned a painting of himself by Andrea Appiani in which he is seated on a throne, dressed in a Roman toga, with a laurel wreath on his head. He had coins minted of himself as the new Caesar, bearing images “almost identical to images of Augustus.” He named his son “king of Rome.” He intended for Paris to be the new Rome. The Arc de Triomphe was modeled after Rome’s Constantine Arch. The Vendome Column, depicting Napoleon’s military victory in Austerlitz, was modeled after Trajan’s Column, which depicted the emperor’s victory over the Dacians. At the top of the Vendome was a statue of Napoleon as the Roman god Mars.

In German, the Roman Empire was called “reich.” Adolph Hitler (1889-1945) intended to establish the Third Reich. He considered Charlemagne’s Holy Roman Empire the First Reich and the German Empire the German Empire under the Hohenzollern royal family of 1871-1918 the Second Reich. Hitler, with his rabid hatred of the Jews, was a preview of the Antichrist. He had the Holy Roman imperial regalia (crown, sword, lance) moved from Vienna to Nuremberg, the unofficial capital of the medieval empire. It was here that the imperial diets (ruling councils) were held. (Over the centuries, many Jews were killed in pogroms in Nuremberg under the Holy Roman emperors, including in 1298 and 1349.) Hitler’s annual rallies in Nuremberg (between 1923 and 1938) imitated the triumph parades of Roman legions. The parade ground was named after Mars, Rome’s god of war. The Nazi standard carried by Hitler’s troops was modeled after the one carried by Roman legions, complete with a red and gold color scheme and a golden eagle on the top. Hitler’s Congress Hall looked like Rome’s Colosseum. The Nazi salute (“Heil Hitler”) was a copy of the Roman salute “Ave Caesar” (“Hail Caesar”). Hitler planned to rebuild Berlin on an east-west axis like Roman cities with a domed building in the center modeled after Hadrian’s Pantheon. What Hitler particularly loved about ancient Rome was its militaristic character and its supposed white “Aryan” racial superiority. He revered the brutal Spartans as “the first racialist state” (Ben Kiernan,

Hitler, Pol Pot, and Hutu Power).

Russia also also aspired to be the Roman Empire. When Constantinople fell to the Muslims in 1453, Moscow became the seat of Greek Orthodoxy. The Russian clergy considered it the “Third Rome.” Emperor Ivan III instigated the use of the term

Tsar(meaning Caesar) and introduced Rome’s double-eagle symbol of authority.

The Roman Empire continues to exist in the unified European nations. In 1957, six nations signed the Treaty of Rome, pledging unity (France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, Luxembourg, and the Netherlands). In 1958, the European Economic Community was born, often called the Common Market. In 1979, an election was held for the first European Parliament. In 1993, the European Union was formed. It encompasses 500 million people and in 2014 owned about 24% of the world’s gross domestic product. In 2002, the Euro was adopted as a common currency. One of the symbols of the European Union is the ancient Tower of Babel. The Tower was featured on a European Union poster in 1992, and the Union’s headquarters in Strasbourg, France, is shaped like an unfinished tower. Another symbol of the Union is the ancient goddess Europa riding a bull, which is a woman riding a beast! See Revelation 17:3. Europa is on the Euro coin, and a statue of her resides outside the Union’s headquarters in Brussels, Belgium. We don’t know if the existing European Union will play any role in the rise of the Antichrist, but we do know that some sort of European Union will. The ten toes of Daniel’s prophecy signify that eventually there will be ten kingdoms within the old Roman Empire, and the Antichrist will assume control and use that base to build his short-lived world kingdom.
