articles.title: Aturan Penerimaan Anggota Gereja Baptis pada Tahun 1828
articles.content:
Berikut ini adalah aturan penerimaan keanggotaan gereja untuk gereja Baptis Charleston, Carolina Selatan, pada tahun 1828. Ini adalah masa ketika gereja-gereja Baptis pada umumnya menganggap keanggotaan dan disiplin gereja dengan serius di hadapan Tuhan Yang Mahakuasa:

1. Apabila seseorang ingin bergabung dengan gereja, keinginan tersebut harus diberitahukan kepada Gembala cukup lama sebelum masa perjamuan Tuhan, untuk memberi kesempatan bercakap-cakap dan berkenalan; dan untuk kepuasan lebih lanjut, Gembala dapat menunjuk diaken, atau saudara-saudara lain yang dianggapnya pantas, untuk mengunjungi Calon tersebut, dengan tujuan memperoleh semua informasi yang diperlukan mengenai pengalaman dan iman, karakter dan kehidupannya.

2. Gembala, dan mereka yang mungkin telah dikirimnya untuk mengunjungi dan bercakap-cakap dengan Calon tersebut, akan bertemu bersama, di tempat yang ditentukannya, untuk mempertimbangkan kualifikasi Calon tersebut, dan setelah pertemuan tersebut, Gembala akan memberikan nasihat kepada masing-masing orang sesuai dengan yang dianggap pantas. Sementara itu, setiap anggota dapat mengunjungi Calon atau Calon-calon tersebut, untuk tujuan berkenalan dan menjalin persekutuan, sebelum masa penerimaan mereka ke dalam gereja.

3. Jika Calon atau Calon-calon tersebut dianggap memiliki kualifikasi yang dapat memberi mereka hak untuk berpartisipasi dalam hak istimewa rumah Allah, mereka harus menghadap Jemaat; yang (karena merupakan taman yang tertutup) akan diadakan secara pribadi untuk tujuan tersebut, dan hanya anggota yang hadir, dan setiap Calon kemudian akan menceritakan alasan harapannya, dan memberikan jawaban atas pertanyaan-pertanyaan mengenai pengetahuan Kristen, pertobatan, dan iman mereka, yang dapat memberikan bukti yang konsisten tentang keadaan yang penuh rahmat; setelah itu, setelah kepuasan diperoleh, mereka akan dibaptis, dan diterima ke dalam semua hak istimewa gereja.

4. Setelah setiap Calon diperiksa di hadapan gereja, ia akan diminta untuk keluar ruangan, sementara Jemaat mempertimbangkan kasus tersebut; Setelah itu, Calon akan dipanggil dan Gembala akan menyampaikan keputusan Jemaat, yang jika menguntungkan, mereka akan diterima dengan baik; tetapi jika tampak ada kekurangan dalam pengetahuan dan pengalaman Calon, dan dianggap lebih baik untuk menunggu beberapa waktu lagi, atau untuk mendapatkan informasi yang lebih baik, Gembala akan, dengan cara yang baik, penuh kasih sayang, dan memberi semangat, menyampaikan saran ini.

5. Dalam hal Calon yang berasal dari pedesaan, atau dalam keadaan khusus yang disebabkan oleh takdir, di mana prosedur di atas tidak dapat dilakukan, Gembala, dan orang-orang yang dia ajak berkonsultasi, harus bertindak sebagaimana yang dianggap paling baik untuk kemuliaan Allah, dan kesejahteraan gereja (John Christian, Sejarah Baptis ).

Calvinism’s Perseverance of the Saints—Why the “P” in T.U.L.I.P. Provides No Assurance of Salvation

By Dr. Andy Woods

Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ. (Romans 5:1)

In this booklet, we will be examining the “P” in the Calvinist T.U.L.I.P. acronym. For the Calvinist, the big question is, how do you know you’re one of the elect? The answer is, you can’t know. You can hope, but you really don’t know unless you get to the end of your life and you are one of those saints who has persevered in doctrine and good works—both of which are very subjective. I mean, how do you know you’ve crossed the finish line? If that’s true of you, then on your dying breath, you can just say, I guess I’m one of the elect because I persevered. But until you reach the end of your life, you really don’t know if you are one of the elect. So, the bottom line in this, as I’ll be showing you, is that there is no assurance of salvation in the Calvinist teaching. And this is what we mean by “perseverance of the saints.”

The Calvinistic Definition of Perseverance of the Saints

With perseverance of the saints, the first thing to understand is we are not talking about eternal security. If all that is meant by perseverance of the saints is the doctrine of eternal security, I would be aligned with them. In fact, one of the things that kept me in Calvinism for a long time was my confusion on this. I thought, Well, I believe in eternal security. Once saved, always saved. So, I’m certainly not Arminian, which teaches that you can lose your salvation. So I must be a Calvinist. Because if you’re a Calvinist, you can’t be an Arminian. And if you’re an Arminian, you can’t be a Calvinist.

That’s how my brain worked. That’s how I was looking at Calvinism for years and years. And it was people like Loraine Boettner, a very Calvinistic teacher and author, who helped confuse me on this where he writes:

It must be evident that there are just two theories which can be maintained by evangelical Christians upon this important subject; that all men who have made any study of it, and who have reached any settled conclusions regarding it, must be either Calvinists or Arminians. There is no other position which a “Christian” can take.1

When I would read this, I would say to myself, I’m certainly not Arminian, so I must be a Calvinist because I believe in eternal security. And in the process, I really didn’t understand what was meant by perseverance of the saints. But in time, I came to see that perseverance of the saints has nothing to do with eternal security. What it has to do with is the notion that you cannot actually believe you’re one of the elect possessing eternal security because nobody knows if they’re going to make it across the finish line.

If you’re one of the elect, it means God infused into you the “gift of faith”2 so that you can believe because you can’t believe any other way because you’re a rock.* And how do you know if your faith is from you or from God? How do you know if it’s an authentic faith, as they call it, or a spurious faith? Well, it always must persevere until the end. How do you know you’re going to persevere until the end? You don’t know until your dying breath. That’s why you can never have assurance of salvation or eternal security in Calvinism. In their book, Calvinism, Hyper-Calvinism, and Arminianism, Talbot and Crampton state:

[I]t should be obvious that the Calvinist doctrine of the perseverance of the saints is not one and the same as “once saved, always saved.”3

Here at Sugar Land Bible Church, we reject the teaching of perseverance of the saints because people can backslide. We reject perseverance of the saints, but we embrace eternal security. It’s important to remember: just because you’re an advocate of eternal security does not make you a Calvinist. What I believe is not in the perseverance of the saints. I believe in the preservation of the saints. What that means is, God preserves you till the end. Now, that puts the onus on who? On God. It takes the onus off who? Off me.

If you want to talk about preservation of the saints, which is a synonym for eternal security, I’m on board with that, but I’m not on board with perseverance of the saints. Peter describes perfectly the preservation of the saints:

To an inheritance incorruptible, and undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for you, Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time. (1 Peter 1:4-5; emphasis added)

This verse is describing how we’re reaching into the next life, an undefiled inheritance. How do I know I’m going to get there and obtain that inheritance? Well, because God has made me a promise that I’m going to get there. That’s how I know. And it has nothing to do with my up days or down days. It has nothing to do with whether I die in a victorious state or not. Because the whole onus is on God’s shoulders, not mine.

Don’t get me wrong; we want to die in a victorious state; that has a bearing on rewards at the Bema Seat Judgment of Christ. Plus, walking in a victorious state allows us to escape a lot of temporal consequences associated with sin. But whether our lives end on an upswing or a downswing, it has nothing to do with our arrival in Heaven because of the doctrine of the preservation of the saints and eternal security.

Now, if you were in a church that was teaching perseverance of the saints, they would call that kind of a statement above heresy. They would basically say I was creating a climate for loose licentious living because in their minds, you have to scare hell out of people every Sunday. The Arminians will scare hell out of you every Sunday by telling you you’re going to lose your salvation. The Calvinists will scare hell out of you every Sunday by telling you that you never had salvation.**

And we wonder why people in the body of Christ are so psychologically and emotionally messed up having these two doctrines rammed down their throats week after week. I’m not going to tell you anything like that because it’s not in the Bible. I’m not going to tell you that you never had salvation. I’m not going to tell you that you lost your salvation. What I’m going to tell you is you’re being kept and protected by the power of God. And whether you die in an upswing or a downswing, it has nothing to do with eternal security because your eternal security never rested on your shoulders to begin with. It wasn’t you that got you in the door. It was the grace of God. So the grace of God that got you in the door is the grace of God that keeps you. Grace means unmerited favor.

Therefore, I have a hundred percent assurance of my salvation because of my right understanding of the preservation of the saints as opposed to the perseverance of the saints. I know one hundred percent that if I were to die today, I’d go to Heaven. Now, I didn’t always think that way because I was an acolyte of the perseverance of the saints, which says, “I don’t know. I’ve got to die on a good note or an upswing, or I’m not in. I don’t have enough proof to demonstrate I’m one of the elect.”

The truth of the matter is our arrival in Heaven and the reception of our heavenly inheritance are being protected by the power of God. Notice that expression, “the power of God” (1 Peter 1:4-5), not the power of you—“the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed at the last time.” So don’t confuse perseverance of the saints with preservation of the saints. Don’t confuse perseverance of the saints with eternal security because those are two completely different teachings. Perseverance of the saints equals perseverance in good works to the end of one’s life to prove he is one of the elect. Bob Kirkland sums up the Calvinist position as follows:

The P [in T.U.L.I.P.] stands for perseverance of the saints. This is what Calvinists say gives them assurance of eternal security but in actuality, “the emphasis is upon the believer’s faithfulness in persevering—not upon God’s keeping power . . . uncertainty as to one’s ultimate salvation is, in fact, built into the very fabric of Calvinism itself.”4

Calvinism teaches uncertainty.

On July 14, 2025, John MacArthur, one of the biggest promoters of Calvinism within evangelicalism, passed away. I remember back when a couple of friends of mine were working on their dissertations and had been given interviews with him; the question was asked, “What is your assurance of salvation on a scale of zero to one hundred?” MacArthur gave a number of about 97 percent. So even the biggest names in Calvinism itself really don’t know if they’re saved. And as they turn around and teach this stuff over and over and over again to the body of Christ, the body of Christ doesn’t know whether they’re saved or not. And that has a massive emotional and psychological negative impact on people.

I’m not a big fan of the integration movement (integrating psychology and the Bible), but Minirth and Meier did a study on this. It was called “The Psychological Effects of Lordship Salvation.”*** They were trying to figure out what this doctrine is doing to people emotionally. It was their conclusion that it was destroying people.5 I’ll use this example by Dennis Rokser: When people were working on the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco when it was being built, there was fear among the workers that they would fall to their deaths. Somebody had a bright idea to put a safety net under these people so they wouldn’t fall to their deaths, and they would feel secure. And guess what they discovered? The productivity of the workers went way up because if you know you’re secure, you’re more productive in your calling. How in the world can you be productive in your calling for Jesus when you don’t even know if you’re going to make it to Heaven or not?6

That kind of teaching is very similar to what you get in Islam, where Muslims really don’t know if they’ve done enough good to outweigh the bad, and they don’t know if Allah, whose name means deceiver, is going to lie to them and rip the carpet out from under them at the final judgment. There is no assurance of salvation in Islam. Once you understand that, you start to have pity on them instead of being mad at them. This is why they would fly a plane into a building. If you fly a plane into a building, that’s a guarantee you’re in. So Muslims do what they do because they have zero assurance of salvation.

How is Calvinism any different in this regard? It is teaching this doctrine of uncertainty, which is emotionally crippling and emotionally destroying people. Because how can you work for Jesus when you don’t trust Him? And if the trust isn’t in Him, maybe I don’t trust myself. Maybe I’m going to mess something up.

So, how can I be productive for God? Well, I’m very productive for God because I’ve got this issue fixed. Jesus is one hundred percent reliable. You might say, “Yeah, but what if I mess things up?” Well, you probably will, and I will, too. But this whole thing doesn’t rest on your shoulders anyway. It’s grace that got you in the door. It’s grace that keeps you in the door. It’s grace that sustains you even when you foul things up.

This is what is meant by the perseverance of the saints. You may be saying, “Well, they don’t really teach this, do they?” That’s why I labored to produce these quotes for you to show you that, yes, they really do teach this.

Examples of Those Who Teach Perseverance of the Saints

John Calvin (1509-1564)
John Calvin writes, “Those who do not persevere unto the end belong not to the calling of God.”7 There it is in black and white. If you don’t persevere till the end (not God preserving you to the end), but if you don’t persevere, then you don’t belong to God because you’re not one of the elect. Calvin also stated:

What they [the Christians at Corinth] had attained so far is nothing, unless they keep steadily on; because it is not enough that they once started off in the way of the Lord, if they do not make an effort to reach the goal.8 (emphasis added)

That looks like the onus is on who? You Corinthians, you started off the right way, Calvin says in his commentary on the Corinthians, but if you guys stumble along the way, you’re not persevering. So whatever faith you had was not real. It was spurious. It was your own faith rather than receiving the gift of faith.

Were the Corinthians saved? Well, what does Paul say at the beginning of the book? “Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, to them that are sanctified” (1 Corinthians 1:2). That sounds pretty spiritual. And “called to be saints, with all that in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours.” (v. 2)

Paul is basically saying, Your salvation, you Corinthians, is just like mine. If you don’t think the Corinthians were saved, then Paul wasn’t saved. See that? It just gets crazy. And as you go through the book of First Corinthians, they weren’t acting very saintly. Chapters one through four, they’re divided over their favorite Bible teachers. Chapter five, they’re involved in incest. Chapter six, they are suing each other in front of unbelieving judges and visiting temple prostitutes. Chapter seven, there’s rampant divorce and remarriage. Chapters eight through ten, those who understood their freedoms in Christ were flaunting their freedoms in the presence of weaker brothers with less understanding, which was causing division. Chapter 11, they’re drunk at the Lord’s table. Chapters 12 through 14, they are all imbalanced in the area of spiritual gifts. They’re putting tongue talkers on a pedestal with no interpretation. And Paul is saying, “If people came into your church right now, they would think you’re stark raving mad.” In chapter 15, they’re throwing overboard the doctrine of the resurrection.

I challenge you to find one place in that whole book where Paul says, “You guys aren’t saved because you’re not persevering.” They had been born spiritually. They were stumbling in growth but not stumbling in birth and being born. Birth truths and growth truths are two different things that Calvinists do not separate.

John Calvin could write a commentary on First Corinthians with all of this powerful language and say, Well, we don’t really know if they’re saved until we see if they persevere in their calling. That’s the perseverance of the saints. Then after that whole mess in the first book of the Corinthians, Paul calls them saints at the beginning of the second book: “Unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints which are in all Achaia.” That’s the same group he just finished talking about. And John Calvin just skipped right over these verses and put a big question mark as to whether these people are saved at all because we don’t know if they’re going to persevere. Now, if they do persevere and they are the elect, then once saved always saved, but we just don’t know if they’re the elect yet because they haven’t persevered.

Paul Washer
Everybody loves Paul Washer. But just because someone has the gift of gab doesn’t mean he’s teaching the right stuff. Just because someone is eloquent on YouTube doesn’t mean he’s arrived at truth. People quote Paul Washer because they like the way he talks. But when Paul Washer talks, he just rehashes over and over and over again this Calvinistic perseverance of the saints. And he says things like, “The doctrine of the carnal Christian has destroyed more lives and sent more people to hell than you can imagine.”9 Now I didn’t know the carnal Christian was a doctrine. Some call it a doctrine; I just call it reading comprehension because the apostle Paul calls the Corinthians carnal, but Washer says it’s a doctrine, meaning that it’s some kind of thing floating around out there. Carnal Christianity is, as much as it’s unfortunate and we don’t promote it, what we would call an unfortunate possibility.

I guess in Paul Washer’s mind, we teach the doctrine of the carnal Christian, and we’re giving people permission to live licentiously, which, of course, proves they’re not one of the elect. That’s what he’s basically saying here. But we don’t promote carnal Christianity. We warn against it. But you can’t warn against something that’s not a possibility. If you really get into what they’re teaching, folks like Paul Washer don’t believe in carnal Christianity. They don’t think it’s such a thing. Yet Paul clearly talks about it in the third chapter of First Corinthians (1 Corinthians 3:1-3).

A.W. Pink (1886-1952)
A.W. Pink said, “Reader, if there is a reserve in your obedience, you are on the way to hell.”10 He means that if God has told you to do something and there’s any hesitancy in your life about it, then that’s just evidence you’re not one of the elect because you’re not persevering. I hope you see that.

To say something like that, A.W. Pink must reject eternal security. Oh, I teach eternal security. I’m just not going to let you know whether you have it or not because I don’t know if you persevered. Of course, he has persevered perfectly, right? We could talk a lot about that. Here’s a guy who died as an angry person at the end of his life, lashing out at everyone in his writings, which you can see if you read them. And what did Jesus say? The standard you use will be used against you. If I took Pink’s standard and used it against him, I could question whether he was a believer or not because I’m not sure he persevered at the end exactly like he should have.

A.W. Pink says this concerning salvation, “Something more than believing in Christ is necessary to ensure the soul’s reaching heaven.”11

So, you believe in Jesus. That’s great. But we’ve got to see more. Well, why do I have to see more? I have to see more because I don’t know if you’re one of the elect or not. I don’t know if you really have the “gift of faith” unless you persevere. Because if you don’t persevere, you were never given the gift of faith by God in the first place. And so, your faith is just your own. And therefore, it’s spurious and not real. Wow. I have no idea why people read this and don’t just denounce it as heretical because to me it’s faith plus what?—perseverance equals salvation.

By the way, is that what Jesus told the thief on the cross? A guy who trusted in Christ at the end of his life. In Luke 23, there’s nothing about you better commit, obey, persevere, serve, get baptized. Jesus just immediately granted him the assurance of salvation upon faith by saying, “ Today shalt thou be with me in paradise” (v. 43).
In his book The Doctrine of Sanctification, Pink writes:

[H]oliness in this life is such a part of our salvation that it is a necessary means to make us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in heavenly light and glory.12 (emphasis in original)

So, according to Pink, if you’re going to get your inheritance in glorification, then we have to see holiness in this life. How much holiness? They don’t say. It’s very subjective. And once you buy into this, you have to spend the rest of your life wondering if you’ve manifested enough holiness. In the verse I gave you earlier (on page 5) from the apostle Peter, you can see that Peter didn’t teach that. Peter taught how God preserves us and keeps us by the “power of God.” Peter never says that this is conditional upon your being on probation. That would make it conditional upon production of holiness. Peter never said that in 1 Peter 1:4-5, but Arthur Pink teaches that.

John Otis
John Otis, a reformed minister, states that “maintaining an unforgiving spirit . . . will surely destroy your souls in hell.”13

So if you’re not following the biblical command to forgive as you’ve been forgiven (Ephesians 4:32), that’s just evidence you’re not one of the elect. And if you die in that state, you’re on your way to hell. Now, should we forgive as we’ve been forgiven? I would recommend it because God told us to do that, and our lives and emotions will be in a lot better state of equilibrium if we live that way. But what if at the end of your life you haven’t yet gotten rid of one of your grudges against somebody who hurt you in the past? And you’re unforgiving towards that person. Well, in John Otis’ eyes, that proves you’re not one of the elect because you’re not persevering. And so you’re in danger of hellfire. This is taking relational forgiveness, and instead of putting it in the category of Christian growth, Christian reward, they’re putting it in the category of Christian birth, which is another gospel.

John Murray (1898-1975)
John Murray, a Calvinist theologian who helped found the Westminster Theological Seminary, writes:

The crucial test of true faith is endurance till the end, abiding in Christ, continuance in the word. . . . He cannot abandon himself to sin.14

Oh, you mean like David did? Yeah, but David came back, didn’t he? Yes, he did. But what if David had died before he came back? Well, he’s out. Murray continues:

He cannot come under the domination of sin. He cannot be guilty of certain kinds of unfaithfulness.15

Certain kinds? What kinds? Are you talking about profanity? Are you talking about an anger problem? Are you talking about gambling? Are you talking about substance abuse? Well, they don’t define it. So the poor sheep are always trying to figure out if they have crossed the line when no one tells them where the line is? They cannot be guilty of “certain kinds of unfaithfulness.” Murray continues:

Let us appreciate the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints and recognize that we may entertain the faith of our security in Christ only as we persevere in faith and holiness to the end.16

Translation: You have no assurance of salvation at all—unless your life is in some kind of upward trajectory spiritually. Your assurance in his mind doesn’t come from God’s promises and God’s commitment to keep you. It comes from your performance. And that performance better be in an upward ascent to the end, or you’re not one of the elect because you haven’t persevered. Murray goes on:

The perseverance of the saints [see how he keeps saying that over and over again] reminds us very forcibly that only those who persevere to the end are truly saints.17

See that word truly? I mean, there’s believers, but who are the true believers? That’s what he’s saying.

That’s why our missions committee here at Sugar Land Bible Church took out some of that language in our missionary questionnaire about truly saved. We don’t use that type of language around here because that’s Calvinistic. You’re either saved, or you’re not. You either have trusted in Christ for salvation, or you haven’t. Calvinists create this whole new category of believers—there are people who believe, but are they truly believers? Maybe it’s just their own faith rather than the gift of faith. And if you start thinking that way, not only does it destroy you individually because you’re always looking at yourself, you’re also not looking at the Cross anymore. It’s always all of this introspection. And I can’t think of a more depressing subject than looking at myself all day long. I mean, I don’t want to look at myself. I want to look at Jesus. But this whole system gets your eyes off Jesus, and it gets them onto yourself. And not only are you looking at yourself all the time, you’re also looking at other people. Uh-oh. Sister so-and-so skipped choir rehearsal two Wednesdays in a row. I don’t know. Maybe she’s not quite in. It leads to this really hypercritical judgmental spirit against other Christians who are having problems.

John MacArthur (1939-2025)
I agree with John MacArthur on many things but disagree with him on the biggest thing, which is the Gospel. He wrote a book called Saved Without a Doubt, which is the most misnamed book in the history of Christianity. If you read his book, you will not think you’re saved without a doubt. You’ll spend your whole life doubting whether you are saved. So, how does John MacArthur give people assurance of salvation? It’s not based on what Jesus promised you at the point of faith. It’s based on what you’re doing. Here is a statement from his book:

If a person fails to love and obey the Lord through the trials of life . . .18

Stop the quote right there. Have you ever gotten discouraged with the Lord on the trials of life? I sure have. I’ve had days where I’m so upset by something going on in my life, I just throw a little pity party. I can identify with people who get upset with the Lord, fail to obey the Lord in the trials of life. Now, when people do that, that’s a growth problem. That’s a rewards issue. That’s not a maybe you’re not a child of God problem because these kinds of things don’t keep you as a child of God. What keeps you as a child of God is God’s promises and God’s grace. And once that net is built (like the one I mentioned earlier under the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco), watch your productivity for the Lord accelerate because you’ve got this issue fixed. But MacArthur says:

If a person fails to love and obey the Lord through the trials of life, then there is no evidence that he or she is a true believer. How many people do you know who followed Christ for a while, had some trouble in their lives, and then went away from him? Although they may have made a profession of faith in Christ, they cannot be identified as those who love Him, because their lives are not characterized by an enduring obedience.19

See what he’s saying here? Their faith isn’t real if they’re not persevering, not enduring, not obedient. And if they’re not persevering, maybe they have spurious faith rather than God’s faith. Maybe they’re not one of the elect. That’s exactly what John MacArthur is saying. All he’s doing is reaching back in years to John Calvin and recycling the perseverance of the saints into modern evangelicalism. And all John Calvin did is reach back over a thousand years and grab these distorted doctrines from Augustine (Augustine being the Catholic’s Catholic).

Charles Hodge (1797-1898)
Calvinist theologian Charles Hodge stated, in referring to evidence of being elected:

The only evidence of election is effectual calling, that is, the production of holiness. And the only evidence of the genuineness of this call and the certainty of our perseverance is a patient continuance in well doing.20

You better be producing holiness, and you better not let it up, or you’re not one of the elect because you’re not persevering. And the only evidence of the “genuineness of this call” means some have true faith, some have false faith.

There it is in black and white by one of Calvinism’s premier theologians—your genuineness, the authenticity of your salvation, is found in your personal subjective life experiences. It’s not on the objective promises of God. It’s on the subjective, which can vacillate from day to day in your own personal experiences.

If someone who is caught up in a cycle of sin comes to me for counseling, the first thing I’m going to ask him is, “Are you saved? Have you ever trusted Christ for salvation?” And if he says he’s never done that, I’m going to try to lead him to salvation through Jesus Christ. But here’s what I’m not going to tell him, “Yeah, I know you’re telling me you’re saved, but you have to prove to me you’re saved because if you don’t prove to me you’re saved, you’re not going to Heaven.” Instead, what I’m going to tell him is, “God has given you resources at the point of faith alone in Christ alone that will help you overcome your cycle of sin. And I exhort you to overcome your cycle of sin because that has a bearing on rewards and a bearing on sparing yourself from a lot of temporal consequences. If you don’t overcome your cycle of sin and you’re telling me you are a saved person, I’m not going to second guess whether you’re saved or not because I know the reality of a non-persevering Christian.” Calvinism says there’s no such thing as a non-persevering Christian. The Bible says there is. Not that it’s good. But it’s what we call an unfortunate possibility.

John Piper
In an article that once sat on his website, Calvinist author and now-retired pastor John Piper said the following:

No Christian can be sure that he is a true believer. Hence there is an ongoing need [perseverance] to be dedicated to the Lord and to deny ourselves so that we might make it.21 (emphasis added)

Just compare that to what Jesus said to the thief on the cross. “Today, you’ll be with me in paradise.” Notice where Piper says “might.” Piper comes along and says, Maybe you’re going to make it. Maybe you’re not going to make it. Because I really don’t know if you’re one of the elect until you persevere till the end.

In an article by Piper that is still on his website today, he says that what he means by the “doctrine of the perseverance of the saints” is that “the saints will and must persevere in faith and the obedience which comes from faith” and that “Our faith must endure to the end if we are to be saved . . . We must endure to the end in faith if we are to be saved.”22 (emphasis in original) The question is, how much persevering and how much enduring must we do? We are not told.

Thomas Schreiner
Thomas Schreiner, a Calvinist academic, introduced something called “final justification.” You’ll find this language of “final justification” or “final salvation” in Schreiner, in John Piper, in Michael Horton,23 and many other Calvinist writers. Schreiner says, “The [New Testament] clearly teaches that bare faith cannot save.”24

Bare faith cannot save? I thought that was the whole deal. Faith alone in Christ alone. I thought that’s what the whole exchange with the thief on the cross was about. I thought the thief on the cross had nothing to offer but trust in the provision of Jesus. And Schreiner comes along and says, that’s not enough.

Schreiner continues in that quote saying that “works are necessary for final justification and final salvation.”25 Isn’t that faith plus works? And what in the world is he talking about here when he says, “final salvation and final justification”? Basically, what it means is information needs to be collected on you throughout the course of your life to determine if the faith you have is really from God. Because if it’s really from God (and remember the Calvinists teach that faith is from God because we are rocks and can’t have faith of our own), it’s always going to endure. It’s always going to persevere. So, what God is doing is He’s collecting data on you as your life progresses. You’re going to get to the very end of your life, and God is going to look at all the data and say, “Check; they’re in. They persevered enough.”

In this Calvinistic view, your justification is not declared at the beginning of salvation, but at the end of salvation. Have you ever heard of such a doctrine? It’s just flatly and patently unbiblical. But this is what Calvinists teach. You get to the end of your life, maybe the good deeds outweighed the bad, and you’re in. Your declaration of innocence doesn’t come at the point of faith like Jesus gave to the thief on the cross. It comes at the end.

What do they say about justification? We say justification is the declaration of innocence that the lost sinner receives at the point of faith in Christ alone. It means we are justified before God. It’s an announcement of our innocence that happens at the beginning of salvation when we first trust in Christ. The Calvinists say, “No, justification actually happens at the end. God is going to collect information on you throughout your Christian life. And if you persevere, demonstrating you’re one of the elect, then you get your grant of justification at the end rather than the beginning.”

And we wonder why so many people in the church have emotional problems and everything else. Well, they have no security. They have no assurance. They have nobody who has built the net, like the one underneath the builders at the Golden Gate Bridge. It’s just tragic.

Eight Problems With the Calvinistic Perseverance Definition

This booklet is taken from my 54-part lecture series on Calvinism. After my introduction to analyzing the P in T.U.L.I.P. (Perseverance of the Saints), on which this booklet is based, I list eight problems with the Calvinistic definition of perseverance of the saints. For an in-depth study on each of these points, I encourage you to watch the series on the Internet (see the links on the copyright page). Below are these eight problems with a brief explanation of each.

  1. Final Salvation is unbiblical. What in the world is this final salvation thing? Well, it’s the idea that information is being stored on you. And if you make it to the end of your life in perseverance, then guess what? You were one of the elect. Your justification is declared about you or to you at the end of the process rather than the beginning. Final salvation is an outworking of the perseverance of the saints.
  2. Scriptural examples of non-persevering saints. One of the easiest ways to debunk this perseverance of the saints doctrine is to show you all the examples in the Bible of people whose salvation is clearly not in doubt. And yet their life didn’t end on a note of victory. At the end of their lives, they obviously weren’t persevering. Yet there’s no doubt they were saved. Some examples from the Old Testament are Noah, Lot, Moses, the Exodus generation, Samson, Saul, Solomon, and there are several examples from the New Testament such as Simon the sorcerer and as I discussed earlier, the believers in Corinth.
  3. Support only found in out-of-context verses. Support for the teaching of perseverance of the saints is found in verses that have been ripped out of their context completely and totally. When someone quotes the Bible, we shouldn’t be overly impressed with that because the devil quotes the Bible (Luke 4:9-12). We have to ask ourselves as good Bereans, are they using the Bible properly? You can make the Bible say whatever you want it to say if you don’t care about context. There are typically seven verses used to support perseverance of the saints.**** But when read in context, none of them have anything to do with the Calvinistic understanding of the perseverance of the saints.
  4. Subtle form of works salvation. The doctrine of perseverance of the saints is actually a subtle form of works salvation: If you really are a Christian and you really are regenerated and you really are saved (and in the Calvinistic way of thinking, if you really are one of the elect), then we need to see commitment, obedience, perseverance, and service. Contrary to that, God gives one condition for eternal life, which is faith in Jesus Christ alone. The Bible says this 160 times.
  5. Preferability of immediate death following conversion. With perseverance of the saints, it would be better if someone just died immediately following conversion because if his life does not end on an upward swing, if he is not persevering enough at the end of his life, then he is not one of the elect.
  6. Lessens the importance of practical sanctification. If the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints is true, and all the elect will ultimately persevere in good works and doctrine, then as a pastor, I do not have to teach on progressive sanctification anymore. I do not have to teach on the need to cooperate with the Holy Spirit via progressive sanctification because it is all going to happen automatically for the elect. And since progressive sanctification is all going to happen automatically for the elect, why waste my time talking about it?
  7. Lessens the importance of the Bema Seat warnings. The Bema Seat Judgment of Christ26 is no big deal if you believe in the perseverance of the saints. According to the perseverance of the saints teaching, everybody (who’s elect) is going to persevere. Everybody gets a participation ribbon. There is nothing to lose. There is nothing to shun. There is nothing to avoid. If I end up a loser at the Bema Seat Judgment of Christ, that just means I was never saved to begin with.
  8. Destroys the assurance of salvation. If you believe in perseverance of the saints, the way the Calvinists teach it, you will go through your whole Christian life with no assurance of salvation because you are always wondering, “Am I persevering enough?” And the Calvinists do not define what the bar is. “Maybe I am not persevering enough.” That is what your mind is satanically open to, once you buy into this perseverance of the saints. You might be crystal clear on eternal security. You might believe in it—“once saved, always saved.” But you just do not know if you have it or not. Perseverance of the saints annihilates the assurance of salvation.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation; but is passed from death unto life. (John 5:24)

*Calvinists erroneously teach that total depravity (the “T” in T.U.L.I.P.) means that man is in some kind of insensate state like a rock unable to respond to God at all even when God convicts them. So God does a work on the front end where He regenerates those who are elect, and He imparts the “gift of faith” because man can’t believe on his own.

**A person receives salvation and eternal life by believing in Jesus Christ alone and trusting in what He accomplished (e.g., Acts 16:30-31; Ephesians 2:8-9)

***Lordship Salvation “refers to that belief which says the sinner who wants to be saved must not only trust Christ as his substitute for sin, but must also surrender every area of his life to the complete control of Christ.” (emphasis added) (see endnote #6 below for source citation)

articles.title: Laba-Laba yang Sangat Cerdas
articles.content:
Sumber: www.creationmoments.com

Selama lebih dari satu abad, para ilmuwan telah bertanya-tanya mengenai hiasan-hiasan yang ditenun oleh setidaknya 78 spesies laba-laba ke dalam jaring mereka. Tambahan berupa garis-garis dan pola berbentuk huruf ‘X’ tersebut tampak tidak memiliki tujuan yang jelas. Beberapa pihak menduga bahwa pola-pola itu mungkin berfungsi sebagai tempat persembunyian, pelindung dari sinar matahari, peringatan bagi burung, atau umpan untuk serangga. Kini, seorang peneliti di Universitas Kyoto mungkin telah menemukan tujuan dari desain-desain tersebut. Jika dugaannya benar, teori evolusi bisa jadi justru ‘terjerat’ oleh jaring laba-laba ini.

Laba-laba Asia yang diteliti oleh peneliti tersebut mampu membuat dua jenis jaring yang berbeda. Saat kenyang, laba-laba ini menambahkan pita-pita sutra di sepanjang jari-jari jaringnya. Namun, saat lapar, ia mengatur pita-pita tersebut hingga membentuk pola spiral yang mengarah ke pusat jaring. Setelah menguji tingkat ketegangan pada kedua jenis jaring tersebut, ia menemukan bahwa jaring dengan pola spiral jauh lebih sensitif — bahkan terhadap serangga terkecil sekalipun — dibandingkan dengan jaring yang hanya memiliki pita-pita biasa. Dengan kata lain, laba-laba yang lapar sedang mencari serangga apa pun yang bisa dimangsa, sementara laba-laba yang kenyang hanya tertarik pada serangga yang lebih besar. Pertanyaannya, bagaimana mungkin evolusi yang tidak berakal dapat memberikan pengetahuan tentang rekayasa struktural yang diperlukan untuk menciptakan desain-desain ini kepada laba-laba? Terlebih lagi, menurut pohon evolusi laba-laba, pengetahuan ini harusnya telah berevolusi setidaknya sembilan kali! Penjelasan yang jauh lebih logis dan lugas adalah bahwa Sang Pencipta memberikan pengetahuan ini kepada laba-laba saat Ia menciptakan mereka.” Ref: Science News, ‘Hungry spiders tune up web jiggliness.’”

articles.title: Kesaksian Seorang Wanita Kristen tentang Cara Berpakaian
articles.content:
Sumber: www.wayoflife.org

Saya sungguh ingin berterima kasih karena Anda telah menulis buku Dressing for the Lord (Berpakaian bagi Tuhan). Buku ini sangat membantu dalam pendalaman Alkitab saya, sehingga saya sampai pada kesimpulan mengenai cara berpakaian. Melalui hal ini, Tuhan benar-benar telah mengubah hati saya dan membuat saya rendah hati. … Hal yang sungguh menyadarkan saya akan kebenaran terjadi saat saya sedang dalam masa pendalaman tersebut. Saya melihat dua pria — di toko yang sama namun pada hari yang berbeda saat saya sedang berbelanja — yang berpakaian dan bertingkah laku layaknya wanita. … sejujurnya, reaksi pertama dalam hati saya adalah rasa jijik dan tersinggung sebagai seorang wanita. Pria-pria ini benar-benar mengolok-olok makna menjadi seorang wanita. Mereka juga membuang jati diri pria yang luar biasa, yang telah dirancang oleh Tuhan bagi mereka. Hal ini membuat saya merasa jijik sekaligus sedih.

Saat menceritakan kejadian ini kepada beberapa teman dan menjelaskan perasaan saya, tiba-tiba terlontar pertanyaan: mungkinkah seperti inilah perasaan kaum pria dahulu, ketika wanita mulai mengenakan celana panjang? Saya pun terdiam dan menyadari bahwa Tuhan baru saja menegur saya melalui perkataan saya sendiri. Pada hari itulah saya memutuskan untuk menyingkirkan celana panjang saya, melakukan perubahan besar, membiarkan rambut saya tumbuh panjang, dan terus membiarkannya tetap panjang. Selain itu, di Irlandia, kami baru saja menyaksikan kaum feminis kembali menang telak dalam pemungutan suara untuk melegalkan aborsi di negara ini. Gerakan feminis ini adalah kelompok yang sama dengan pihak yang memelopori penggunaan celana panjang bagi wanita, yang secara vokal dan gencar mendorong paham androgini serta homoseksualitas. Mereka bahkan berpawai di Washington DC dengan mengenakan pakaian yang vulgar dan menjijikkan demi memperjuangkan aborsi, dan kini mereka terus mendorong praktik aborsi di seluruh dunia.

Jika orang-orang yang mendukung pembunuhan massal terhadap anak-anak tak berdosa—serta memicu kebingungan gender dan merusak rancangan Tuhan — adalah kelompok yang sama dengan pihak yang memulai tren memotong rambut wanita menjadi pendek dan mengenakan celana panjang, maka saya ingin menegaskan kepada siapa pun yang melihat saya bahwa saya sama sekali tidak terlibat dalam kejahatan ini.

Setelah memutuskan untuk berhenti mengenakan celana panjang, Tuhan menunjukkan kepada saya bahwa kesantunan dalam berpakaian — dengan mengenakan busana layaknya seorang wanita — berkaitan dengan sesuatu yang jauh lebih dalam di dalam hati. Hal ini merupakan simbol kerendahan hati. Ini tentang belajar untuk memiliki roh yang lemah lembut dan tenang. Ini tentang mengakui serta menghormati otoritas yang ditetapkan Tuhan dalam hidup kita, dan merasa puas menjadi sosok sebagaimana Tuhan menciptakan kita — yang merupakan jati diri terbaik bagi kita. Saat saya mengenakan rok panjang yang longgar dan menutup bagian tubuh yang memang seharusnya tertutup, saya sedang dengan rendah hati tunduk kepada Tuhan dan kepada otoritas yang telah Ia tetapkan dalam hidup saya. Saya telah belajar bahwa dalam ketundukan tersebut, saya terlindungi, baik secara rohani maupun jasmani.

articles.title: Kristus Palsu Versi Kid Rock
articles.content:
Sumber: www.wayoflife.org

“Tetapi aku takut, jangan-jangan sebagaimana sang ular telah menipu Hawa dengan kelicikannya, demikian juga pikiran kalian telah diselewengkan dari kesederhanaan yang ada dalam Kristus. 4 Sebab jika seseorang datang memberitakan Yesus yang lain, yang tidak pernah kami beritakan, atau jika kalian mendapatkan roh yang lain, yang tidak kalian terima sebelumnya, atau injil yang lain yang tidak kalian sambut sebelumnya, kalian begitu sabar membiarkannya” (2 Korintus 11:3-4).

Kid Rock (nama aslinya Robert Ritchie) — yang begitu membanggakan musik rock & roll yang kotor hingga ia menjadikannya sebagai nama panggungnya — memiliki album baru berjudul Halfway 2 Jesus. Rapper yang tercela, Eminem, turut tampil sebagai bintang tamu. (Kid Rock dikenal luas karena gaya hidupnya yang penuh pesta pora, perzinaan, kekerasan, kata-kata kasar, serta penyalahgunaan narkoba dan alkohol; ia mendukung aborsi, pernikahan sesama jenis, dan legalisasi narkoba. Album-album sebelumnya antara lain Devil Without a Cause, Cocky, Rebel Soul, Early Mornin’ Stoned Pimp, dan Bad Reputation.)

Dalam sebuah wawancara baru-baru ini dengan Lara, menantu Presiden Trump, Kid Rock menjelaskan kekristenannya sebagai berikut: “Setelah Charlie Kirk dibunuh, seperti banyak orang lainnya, saya mulai merasa lebih dekat dengan iman saya. Jadi, saya mulai menulis lagu-lagu ini, dan tiba-tiba saja lagu-lagu itu datang begitu saja kepada saya. Saya paham mengapa ada skeptisisme. Orang-orang bertanya, ‘Apakah Kid Rock sudah diselamatkan?’ Maksud saya, saya tidak ‘diselamatkan.’ Saya tetaplah Kid Rock. Saya masih akan minum bir dan mengisap cerutu. Saya merasa selama ini hubungan saya dengan Tuhan sudah baik-baik saja.”

Perhatikan bahwa Kid Rock secara terus terang menyatakan bahwa ia tidak mengalami keselamatan dan tidak mengubah gaya hidupnya. Ia mengeklaim bahwa hubungannya dengan Tuhan selalu baik, yang berarti ia tidak pernah mengalami pertobatan — tidak pernah beralih dari kematian menuju kehidupan, atau dari kegelapan menuju terang. Alkitab menyatakan, “Jadi jika seseorang berada dalam Kristus, ia adalah ciptaan baru, hal-hal lama sudah berlalu, sesungguhnya segala sesuatu telah menjadi baru” (2 Kor. 5:17). Alkitab juga mengatakan, “Mereka mengaku mengenal Allah, tetapi mereka memungkiri Dia melalui pekerjaan-pekerjaan mereka, karena mereka keji dan durhaka dan terbukti gagal dalam setiap hal yang baik” (Titus 1:16).

Yesus versi Kid Rock adalah Kristus palsu yang — berbeda dengan Kristus dalam Kitab Suci — tidak menyerukan pertobatan (Luk. 3:1-5) maupun kelahiran baru (Yoh. 3:1-8). Ia tidak menuntut penyangkalan diri (Mat. 16:24), serta tidak memberikan peringatan mengenai api neraka yang kekal (Mat. 5:22; 7:19; 13:40, 42, 50; 18:8, 9; 25:41), iblis (Yoh. 8:44), pengajar palsu (Mat. 7:15-20), ataupun kekristenan palsu (Mat. 7:21-23). ??Yesus versi Kid Rock adalah Yesus ala pop Amerika, Yesus versi Fox News, atau Yesus versi politik konservatif yang menerima segala hal yang berlabel “Kristen”: sakramentalisme, baptisan bayi, keselamatan sebagai sebuah proses, kekristenan yang mendukung homoseksualitas, kepausan, adorasi hosti, venerasi kepada orang kudus, doa kepada Maria, fenomena dibunuh dalam Roh, praktik “bahasa roh” yang tidak dapat dipahami, pendeta perempuan, serta gaya hidup yang menuruti hawa nafsu pribadi.

The Authenticity of the Book of Joshua(2015).

Bill Cooper (1947-2021) was was a prolific writer and speaker, with a gift of cutting through the fog of biblical criticism to defend the infallible, plenary, verbal inspiration of Scripture, the six-day creation, and the Masoretic Hebrew and Received Greek texts. He was a council member of the Creation Science Movement and the Tyndale Society and an adjunct professor for the Institute for Creation Research’s Master Faculty. His most popular book is

After the Floodwhich gives evidence for the historicity of Genesis 10 based on ancient, little known British and European genealogies. He published a series of books entitled “The Authenticity,” which included The Authenticity of the Book of Genesis, Joshua, Judges, Esther, Daniel, Jonah, the Gospels, Acts, the Epistles, and Revelation. In

The Forging of Codex Sinaiticus, Cooper gave evidence to support his thesis that Sinaiticus is a forgery.

Cooper was a careful researcher, an independent thinker, and a brave defender of God’s eternal truth. He accomplished this in spite of suffering serious illnesses, including leukemia, the last two decades of his life. We can’t agree with all of his conclusions; at times he seems to be dogmatic when the evidence isn’t absolute; there are a few occasions when he might have been led astray by Jewish mysticism; but everything we have read from his pen is well worth considering.

If you want to be encouraged in your faith in the divine inspiration of Scripture, read Bill Cooper.

Ten of Cooper’s books are available in print from Gullion’s Christian Supply (King and Statesville, NC)

https://www.gullions.com/contact-us

https://www.4gospel.com/bill-cooper/

All of Cooper’s books are available in Kindle format from Amazon.

___________


To read the critics, you’d think that the records of 15th-century BC Canaan would have nothing to say either about Joshua or his people. They will tell you that that is because Joshua himself did not exist, and his people never conquered the land called Canaan. It was all just a myth cobbled together by the wishful thinking of Jewish ‘editors’ after their return from the Babylonian Exile. And this is not some outdated allegation which has been corrected recently as scholarship has improved over the years. It is being made increasingly even today by some of the major critics and taken up by the media and universities. It is therefore with considerable surprise that we read about Joshua and his people, not just once in some ambiguous, fragmentary inscription of dubious date and interpretation, but plainly and at least 85 times in that 15th-century BC Canaanite archive known as the Tell El Amarna Tablets. The critics don’t like to mention the fact, but Joshua himself is sometimes obliquely referred to in the Tablets. There is one man in particular who is referred to as ‘that Hebrew’; ‘that Hebrew dog’; at least three times as the ‘chief of the Hebrews’; and, it seems, in one inscription he is called ‘Ilimilku,’ which name is the Akkadian cognate of the Hebrew name Elimelech, God is my King. It is a nickname which would have suggested itself to Canaanite observers after it became clear to them that Joshua was not a king, but that he fought under the God of Israel. Though not a name that the Bible specifically gives him, it is one that the Canaanites seem to have known him by, and they accordingly wrote it down in their correspondence - ‘Ilimilku!’1
The Hebrews themselves are referred to in the Amarna Tablets as slaves – ‘runaway dogs’ in some of the Tablets – ‘slaves that have become Habiru’ in another - recalling the history of their escape from slavery in Egypt. This again is entirely natural and to be expected. After all, if Rahab, a mere harlot of Jericho, was familiar with this history (Joshua 2:9-11), why should the much better informed kings of Canaan not have been? A trawl through the Amarna archive reveals the following references to Joshua and his people. It does not include every instance in which the Hebrews or their leader are mentioned, but it does give us a good idea of just how prominently Joshua and his people figured on the Canaanite scene. The incursion of the Hebrews was indeed a major invasion, and its startling impact on the Canaanite kings comes over loud and clear in the urgency of their appeals to the Pharaoh of Egypt to send soldiers to help fight them off.
This is evidence for the integrity of the Book of Joshua that is of the very highest quality, and it is astonishing that this information has not been made more available to the public.
What has been made available is the somewhat inaccurate notion that a couple of the tablets mention some “Apiru,” a name which, we are asked to believe, may be derived from the Assyrian word habbatu, meaning robber, and that these occurrences must therefore refer to some troublesome bandits that were roaming the area at that time.
Nothing could be more distorted and inaccurate. It is a forced and false derivation which misleads the reader. The Canaanite kings were certainly strong enough and well enough organised to see off any such bands of robbers, whom they would have hunted to extinction. It is what they did, and they were very good at it. Canaan could never have become a land flowing with milk and honey had it been a land in which lawless bands of cutthroats carried the day. Neither do bands of robbers capture whole swathes of territories along with their walled and fortified cities which were protected by regiments of disciplined and armed soldiers.
No. The term Apiru, which appears throughout the archive, is merely the Akkadian cognate of the word Hebrew (Habiru), Akkadian being the diplomatic language in which most of the tablets are written.
The critics know this very well, and those who deliberately disguise the meaning and hide it from the public - which many of them have done since the archive’s discovery in 1887 - commit a very grave offence indeed.
To counter this concerted misrepresentation, in the quotes below we have rendered the Akkadian word Apiru in all places into its proper meaning of Hebrew, or Hebrews. This will allow the reader to see the contents of the tablets in their correct historical context and perspective.
The quotes below are not from one, but from many Canaanite kings, each of them complaining in turn that as the Hebrews come closer to them, so their danger increases. At the end of each quote, we give the tablet number and the line of text in which the quote appears. It is not a complete list of the occurrences, nor can we be at all sure that the tablets have been catalogued in their correct chronological order. In fact the order appears to have been inverted for some reason, a matter which we will discuss a little later.
In the Appendices, we give the full text of some of the Amarna letters, so that the reader can better judge the context in which certain of the quotes below are given:
[Cooper’s quotes from the Armada Letters can be found in his book The Authenticity of the Book of Joshua.]
...
But there are added corroborations for the Book of Joshua amongst the Amarna Tablets, and one of them is the specific mention of “men of Judah” – ameluti Ia-u-du! – and “armed men [or warriors] of Judah” – ameluti sabe Ia-u-du.2 The Canaanite spelling of Ia-u-du is identical to that of Assyrian inscriptions which later speak of Judah, and it is interesting to see the men of Judah and the many cities allotted to Judah set out so precisely in Joshua 15. The tribe of Judah formed a major component of Joshua’s people, and it is interesting to see the Canaanites unwittingly acknowledging that fact.
It is also worth noting a complaint made by Abdi-heba, king of Jerusalem, that he is troubled by the men of “Laba,” or Levi in the Hebrew.3 Malchiel and Heber (Numbers 26:45), clans descended from the Hebrew tribe of Asher, also figure in Abdi-heba’s complaints as the ‘sons of Milkil’,4 and it is these important details which give the lie to the critics’ claim that the Apiru of the Amarna Tablets are not Hebrews but bands of Bedouin raiders. Bedouin were never called ‘men of Judah,’ ‘Malchielites’ or ‘Heberites’ by anyone, not in Canaan or anywhere else, and it is most disappointing that the critics don’t seem to know that fact. Perhaps one of them would like to explain why they don’t know it?
But for such a major portion of the Amarna archive to be taken up with such urgent pleas for military help from Egypt against the Hebrews - and men of Judah! - it is clear that we are not here dealing with bands of robbers. Such roving thieves were dealt with on a daily basis throughout the Middle East, and their suppression certainly did not require pleas for international military assistance. Neither did they ever reduce so many kings at once to a state of abject panic, confusion and despair. No. The Hebrews – the people of the Book of Joshua and the Apiru of the Amarna Tablets – were one and the same, and were much more than mere robbers. They were a formidable and devastating military presence who were systematically and successfully overrunning the land, and they were not about to go away.
When we read of these things in the Amarna Tablets, we see the truth of Rahab’s words to the spies when she said to them: “I know that the LORD hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed. And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man because of you....” Joshua 2:9-11. These words were not written by some Jewish propagandist composing his lie a full one thousand years after the event. We read the Tablets, and we read Rahab’s words, and we see at once that her words are authentic, reflecting exactly the reality of what was occurring in her own day and in her land of Canaan. The Canaanite kings have left their own vociferous testimony to the truth of the Book of Joshua, and it is no exaggeration to say that, had the invasion of Canaan under Joshua not taken place – as the critics claim - then the Amarna archive would never have carried this independent testimony to the fact that the Hebrews – including men of Judah, Levites, Malchielites and Heberites! - successfully invaded and overran Canaan in the late 15th century BC, the very time in which the archive’s contents were written. And we must remember that the archive’s letters were not written and sent by just one of Canaan’s kings, but by many.
...
The story begins with the publication in 1893 of Major C R Conder’s The Tell Amarna Tablets.3 Conder was a Bible believer who was more than happy to point out to the reading public how the latest archaeological discoveries corroborated the Bible. Hence he saw no difficulty whatever in transliterating and translating – and then publishing - Biblical names whenever he came across them. Happily for Bible apologists, he was able to translate the Amarna Tablets before the modernist critics moved in and brought down the shutters. They were too late, of course. Apart from the fall of Jericho, Conder had already informed the public that: “The names of Japhia, King of Gezer; of Jabin, King of Hazor; and, probably, Adonizedek, King of Jerusalem - contemporaries of Joshua – occur among those of the writers.”4 Each of these personages and the cities which they ruled (including Jericho), are known to us from the Book of Joshua itself. Naturally, Bible apologists were delighted with the news. One amongst many was the Rev. Thomas Harrison, Fellow of the Royal Geographical Society, Member of the Society of Biblical Archaeology, and Senior Lecturer to the Palestine Exploration Fund – and so on, not an unimportant voice in those days. On May 19th 1893, he greeted Conder’s translation of the Tablets in these welcoming terms: “It is certainly very interesting to find in the letters the names of Japhia (Josh. x., 3, one of the kings killed by Joshua) and most probably that of Adonizedek, king of Jerusalem; while the name of a king of Hazor is read as Jabin (Josh. xi., 1).... Many matters of great interest in connection with these tablets can find no mention within the limits of this paper. It may be added, however, that the topographical value of these letters is very great; and also that the evidence which they afford as to the Hebrew conquest of Palestine under Joshua is in favor of the Bible chronology (Acts xiii., 20; I. Kings vi., 1) and against that of Dr. Brugsch and Bunsen.”5
It could not have been worse news for the critics. Their denigration of the Scriptures was almost in full swing, and this kind of information reaching the public could undo decades of hard work. Then as now, the critics had only one agenda, and that was to destroy the credibility of the Bible in the public imagination. The Amarna archive threatened that agenda very seriously indeed, and it is interesting to see how the damage was limited. The first to tell us about what happened is one Robert Harper whom we have met elsewhere:6 “The Tel-el-Amarna tablets in the British Museum are marked Bu. 88- 10- 13+ or, Budge the 13th of October, 1888. Students have inquired for these tablets ever since their arrival in the British Museum, but the answer given was, "they are reserved for official use." Later on it became known that Drs. Bezold and Budge were preparing an edition of this collection.”
They were indeed, and their edition appeared in 1892.8 Bezold and Budge would have known that Conder had been translating the tablets – he had been working under their very noses - and they would have known by reputation where his sympathies lay concerning the Bible. It was essential therefore that their edition pre-empted the news that Conder was about to release, and so, bringing out their – untranslated! - edition of the tablets in 1892, the year before Conder published his translation, they were careful in their jointly-written preface to avoid all suggestion that the Book of Joshua was in any way exonerated by the Amarna archive. Not once is the Hebrew invasion of Canaan referred to, and the Old Testament in general is only briefly acknowledged merely for the fact that its Hebrew is related to the language of the tablets. They were laying the ground for what was to follow.
E A Wallace Budge is also known to us elsewhere for his public denigration of the Assyriologist George Smith, who, like Conder after him (he died in 1876), was not averse to advertising to the public any and every occasion on which he found the Bible exonerated in the Assyrian inscriptions.9 Wallace Budge was a thoroughly godless man with a strong anti-Biblical bias. Wrapped in spiritualism and an active member of the occult, he was placed by the British Museum in a position of great authority, being able to censor any of the Museum’s publications before they went to press. And so it is that under him all information exonerating the Bible or any part of it was actively and conscientiously suppressed. Hence, in his edition of the Amarna archive, any sympathetic, exonerating reference to the Bible and to the Book of Joshua in particular is avoided.
...
“In his Rise and Progress of Assyriology (1925), Wallace Budge attempted to portray George Smith nearly fifty years after his death as an emotionally-charged buffoon who was unfitted for the tasks appointed him (Damrosch, pp. 64-80), forgetting that from 1872 onwards Smith had taken him under his wing and had taught him the Assyrian language, in spite of his own horrendous workload. Wallace Budge, in other words, owed the launch of his career to George Smith’s Christian kindness and patience. But Wallace Budge was no stranger to slandering his friends and colleagues, and in 1893 was even sued for it. But then, paying no more than faint lip service to ‘liberal Christianity’ whilst he pursued his spiritualism, there was little to restrain or improve him. His interests turned from Assyriology to Egyptology because, like himself, the Egyptians had little to say about the Bible, and they worshipped the dead. Admired by Blavatsky, the founder of the Theosophical (Luciferian) Society; involved in the Ghost Club, the spiritualist ‘church’ founded in 1862 by the apostate Bible critics Westcott and Hort; and a member of the occultic Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn, Wallace Budge was steeped in devilry – and this was the man that the British Museum selected to replace George Smith. It hardly bears thinking about.” Authenticity of the Book of Genesis, p. 209. – see also p. 202.

articles.title: Evidence at the Shrine of the Book
articles.content:
866-295-4143,

fbns@wayoflife.org

Jews in Fighter Jets: Israel Past, Present, and Future, which is available from Way of Life Literature in print and eBook editions.

They are the keepers of both the Great Isaiah Scroll and the Aleppo Codex.

The Masoretic text was preserved by Hebrew scribes prior to the invention of printing by moveable type in the 15th century. (The first printed Hebrew Bible appeared in 1488.)

The Shrine of the Book was opened in 1965 by the Israel Museum, only 17 years after the War of Independence. Its national importance is evident by the fact that it is located in a prominent place in Jerusalem near the Israeli Parliament (the Knesset).

The roof of the museum is in the shape of the lid of the clay jars that protected the Dead Sea Scrolls, and the corridor leading into the museum resembles a cave. The brilliant white of the museum’s roof contrasts sharply with the black wall nearby, signifying the warfare between the Sons of Light and the Sons of Darkness described in writings of the Essenes community found among the Dead Sea Scrolls. The Essenes cult wrongly thought of itself as the true Sons of Light, and the modern state of Israel does not understand the real significance of such things. But the Bible held in the Shrine of the Book teaches that there

isa war between truth and error, light and darkness, and that it will culminate at the return of Christ.

It is most amazing and wonderful that the two greatest witnesses to the authenticity of the Masoretic Bible are located in the Jewish Shrine of the Book in the modern state of Israel, because it was to the Jews that God assigned the task of preserving the Hebrew Bible. In Romans 3:1-2 Paul calls the Hebrew Old Testament the “oracles of God” (“oracles” means utterance), and tells us that these oracles were committed to the Jews. Though the Jews did not obey the Scripture, they revered it. Josephus and Philo “assure us that they would have undergone all sorts of torments rather than have taken a letter from the Scripture, or altered a word of it” (John Kitto,

Illustrated History of the Bible, edited by Alvan Bond, 1908, p. 39). Countless Jews have died in their zeal to protect and preserve the Old Testament Scripture.

This reverence was placed in their hearts by the God of the Bible for the purpose of its preservation.

In particular, it was the Jewish priests who were assigned as the keepers of the Scriptures (Deut. 31:24-26; 17:18).

After the Babylonian captivity there was a revival within the Jewish priesthood (Ezra 7:10) and the Old Testament Scriptures were preserved. “By Ezra and his successors, under the guidance of the Holy Spirit, all the Old Testament books were gathered together into one Old Testament canon, and their texts were purged of errors and preserved until the days of our Lord’s earthly ministry. By that time the Old Testament text was so firmly established that even the Jews’ rejection of Christ could not disturb it” (Dr. Edward Hills,

The King James Bible Defended, 4th edition, p. 93).

Following the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70, it was Jewish rabbis called

Tannaim(teachers) who guarded the Old Testament Scriptures. These scribes “copied the text of the Old Testament with great accuracy” (Edward Hills,

The King James Bible Defended, 4th edition, p. 93). The

Tannaimwere followed by the other scribes called

Amoraim(expositors). Though they exalted Pharisaical tradition above Scripture in practice, they highly revered the Scripture and preserved it from generation to generation. (It was during this time that the Talmud was produced, which canonized the very type of rabbinical tradition that Jesus condemned in Matthew 15:3-9.)

Beginning in the sixth century, it was THE MASORETES (traditionalists) who jealously guarded the Hebrew text and passed it down from generation to generation. It is the Masoretic Hebrew Bible that was adopted by Christians and used in the first printed Bibles.

The Masoretes were families of Hebrew scholars who were based in Tiberias after the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 135 by Rome at the end of the Second Jewish War. The traditional Hebrew Masoretic text gets its name from these scholars.

The most famous Masorete was Ben Asher, who “labored to produce a correct copy of the Scriptures.” From the 12th century forward the Ben Asher text was the received Hebrew Bible.

Fearful of losing the correct verbalization of the Hebrew words through the Jewish dispersion, the Masoretes added verbalization marks to the text.

The Masoretes exercised great care in transcribing the Old Testament. They developed stringent rules for copying in order to keep the text pure. The following rules are from

General Biblical Introductionby Herbert Miller (1937), with information added from other sources.

  • The parchment must be made from the skin of clean animals; must be prepared by a Jew only, and the skins must be fastened together by strings taken from clean animals.
  • Each column must have no less than 48 nor more than 60 lines. The entire copy must be first lined.
  • The ink must be of no other color than black, and it must be prepared according to a special recipe.
  • No word or letter could be written from memory; the scribe must have an authentic copy before him, and he must read and pronounce aloud each word before writing it.
  • He must reverently wipe his pen each time before writing the word for “God” (Elohim) and he must wash his whole body before writing the name “Jehovah” lest the Holy Name be contaminated.
  • Every word and every letter was counted, and if a letter was omitted, an extra letter inserted, or if one letter touched another, that section of the manuscript was condemned and destroyed. A Masoretic Hebrew manuscript of Genesis contains 4,395 lines in 43 columns, with 27,713 words and 78,100 letters.

Miller concludes with this observation: “Some of these rules may appear extreme and absurd, yet they show how sacred the Holy Word of the Old Testament was to its custodians, the Jews (Rom. 3:2), and they give us strong encouragement to believe that WE HAVE THE REAL OLD TESTAMENT, THE SAME ONE WHICH OUR LORD HAD AND WHICH WAS ORIGINALLY GIVEN BY INSPIRATION OF GOD” (

General Biblical Introduction, 1937, p. 185).

The Great Isaiah Scroll

The Great Isaiah Scroll was found in Cave 1 at Qumran near the Dead Sea in 1947. It contains the entire book of Isaiah. It was written on 17 pieces of sheepskin sewn together to form a scroll measuring about 24 feet in length. It resides at the Shrine of the Book, and a realistic facsimile is on display in the main room. It has been dated at least four times by the carbon-14 method and the results have ranged from 335 to 107 BC. Other dating techniques (e.g., writing material and style, associated artifacts) have dated it to 150-100 BC. Thus it was written at least a century before Christ, if not two or three centuries.

Every book of the Old Testament was found in the Dead Sea Scrolls except the book of Esther, and sixty to sixty-five percent of the scrolls represent the Masoretic text. This is amazing since the earliest Hebrew codexes of the Masoretic text used by scholars in the 16th and 17th centuries (such as the Aleppo) were written more than a thousand years after the Dead Sea Scrolls. The differences between the conservative Dead Sea scrolls and the Masoretic text are extremely minor, largely pertaining to spelling or grammar, the omission or addition of a word, or the mixing of Hebrew letters. For example, one of the two Isaiah scrolls found in Cave 1 leaves out one “holy” from Isaiah 6:3, obviously a scribal oversight. Comparing Isaiah 53 in the Great Isaiah Scroll of 100 BC and the Apello Codex of AD 900, there are only three letters that differ. As for the Great Isaiah Scroll and its agreement with the Masoretic text, Dr. Ernst Wurthwein calls it “striking” and Adolfo Roitman calls it “extraordinarily close” (Wurthwein,

The Text of the Old Testament, 1979, p. 144; Roitman,

The Bible in the Shrine of the Book, 2006, p. 43).

The Aleppo Codex

The other great witness to the authority of the Masoretic Hebrew Bible at the Shrine of the Book is the Aleppo Codex (known in Hebrew as

Ha-Keter, meaning

the Crown). It was made in about AD 900-920 in Tiberias, which became the center of Jewish scholarship in Israel after the razing of Jerusalem.

The Aleppo manuscript was copied by Shlomo (Solomon) Ben Boya’a, and the vowel markings were added by Aaron ben Asher.

For nearly 1,000 years it “was used as the standard text in the correction of books” while “generations of scribes made pilgrimages to consult” it (Roitman, p. 62).

About 100 years after it was completed, it was given as a gift to the Jews in Jerusalem. After the Roman Crusaders conquered Jerusalem in 1099 and established the Crusader kingdom, they captured the Codex and took it to Egypt, where it was purchased by the Jews.

It resided at a synagogue in Cairo until 1375, when it was moved to the synagogue in Aleppo, Syria. There it resided in a double-locked metal box in “the Cave of Elijah” (according to Jewish tradition, Elijah was exiled there). The keys were held by two prominent men and the box could only be opened in the presence of both men on the authority of the synagogue’s leaders. It was used as the touchstone of Hebrew Bible purity.

On December 2, 1947, after the adoption of the UN resolution authorizing the establishment of the Jewish state, the Aleppo synagogue was destroyed by rampaging Muslims during the riots that broke out all over the Arab world. The rioters broke into the iron box and ripped pages from the Codex and threw it on the floor. Most of the Pentateuch was lost, as well as some other portions. Someone recovered the damaged Codex, and it was hidden for the next several years. In 1958 it was smuggled to Turkey hidden in a washing machine, and from there brought to Jerusalem. It was laboriously restored over a six-year period by the Israel Museum and today is on display in the Shrine of the Book.

Scholars now admit that the Masoretic text was the standard Hebrew Bible at the end of the Second Temple period. This has been proven not only by the Dead Sea Scrolls but also by scrolls found at Masada, Wadi Murabba’at, Nahal Hever, and Nahal Tze’elim. Adolfo Roitman says the Masoretic “apparently became the authoritative text for mainstream Judaism toward the end of the Second Temple period” (

The Bible and the Shrine of the Book, p. 56).

In light of Romans 3:1-2, that is a major admission! Liberal scholars see the Masoretic text and the competing Septuagint and Samaritan texts as representing equally legitimate texts. They believe it is only because the rabbis banned the former that the Masoretic text won out. They see it as an accident of history. For example, Geza Vermes says, “[The existence of both Masoretic and Septuagint texts in the Dead Sea Scrolls] suggests that in the Qumran age Hebrew texts corresponding to the Samaritan and the ancient Greek versions jointly circulated, thus buttressing the theory that the proto-Masoretic, Samaritan and Septuagint-type of Hebrew text forms happily co-existed before rabbinic censorship eliminated the last two around 100 CE” (

The Story of the Scrolls, p. 106).

This is almost exactly what liberal New Testament scholars believe about the Alexandrian Greek text. They think that the Traditional Greek Text underlying the Protestant Bibles won out merely because it was proclaimed official by church councils and pushed by church authorities. They hold this view because they do not believe that the Old and New Testaments were given by divine inspiration and preserved by the same God who authored them. The Bible to them is a purely human product, and in studying it they only consider the human element.

But in light of Paul’s statement in Romans 3:1-2 and the many promises in Scripture that God would preserve His Word, we know that God was superintending the transmission of the Old Testament, and God led the Jewish rabbis, even in their unbelief and spiritual blindness, to preserve the Masoretic Bible. (For an extensive study on Bible preservation see our book

Faith vs. the Modern Bible Versions.)

The Jewish authorities that operate the Shrine of the Book believe that the exhibition of the Aleppo Codex is the fulfillment of Isaiah 2:3: “... for out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem” (“The Wandering Book: The Aleppo Codex”).

In fact, this great prophecy will be fulfilled at the return of Christ when “the mountain of the LORD’s house shall be established in the top of the mountains, and shall be exalted above the hills; and all nations shall flow unto it” (Isaiah 2:2). It is obvious that this does not refer to our day when Israel is one of the most despised of nations on the face of the earth!

Both the Great Isaiah Scroll and the Aleppo Codex have been digitized and are available at the Israel Museum’s web site: http://www.imj.org.il/shrine_center/
